I know most of the above has already been said, but this is just my two cents on the subject.

#32259 10 2004-10-16T22:12:50Z tktktk
Dustman, here are a few suggestions...

1. Start out with a general idea of what your level is going to be like.

2. Don't hide objects (such as the exit switch in this level).

3. Make sure every object you place in your level has a specific purpose.

4. Play through your levels, and as you do, ask yourself what parts are fun and what parts are unnecessary or frustrating.

Hope this helps and good luck with future maps!

#1330 1 2004-11-11T22:53:15Z tktktk
I wrote this essay for english class. The assignment was to write a 250-word essay including a flashback. As you read it, keep in mind that I purposely made it very vague. You have to use a little imagination to fill in the gaps in the story. Here it is:

The man in the rocking chair had no future. After sitting and thinking for a long time, he came to this conclusion. It was not because of anything he had done in the past at least, not on purpose. But after endlessly thinking over what had brought him to this point, he realized that it was all because of one fateful day, many years ago.

It had been bright and cheery that morning, but he had been in no mood to perform his duties. He convinced himself that the classified units wouldnt come to any harm. After all, what could happen? He was only one of several dozen keeping watch over the units. If there was a break-in, which was quite unlikely to begin with, surely there would be some warning. With this thought in mind, he drifted off into a light slumber. Suddenly he awoke with a start, immediately realizing something was amiss. He ran through the halls, shouting for someone, anyone but the complex was deserted. After a few moments of trying to steady himself, he worked up the courage to check on the units. He had never actually seen them before; no one but the highest-ranking officials were allowed in the room. He found the door unlocked. He opened it.

As the man in the rocking chair recalled that day, which had forever altered both his life and the lives of countless others, he knew what he had to do. He got up, and slowly set to work. Soon the future he once had would be restored.

This isn't my usual writing style, I'm trying something new. Any feedback would be greatly appreciated. It's okay if you just hate it, I would still like to know.

Quote: TornadoTK, 2004-11-18T06:37:51Z
Also, the comment they made comparing gaming to operating systems didn't make too much sense. If XBox can bang over Nintendo Gamecube in consoles (still #2 compared to PS2), why can't PSP kick the DS to the curb?
Because Nintendo has had complete control over the handheld market for the last 15 years.

By the way, the another major problem with the PSP is its short battery life. 4 to 6 hours really doesn't cut it. Plus, it'll be even less than that for action-oriented games like Ridge Racer, and for watching movies.

If there's one good thing about the PSP, though it's the price. Even though it's about $40 more expensive than the DS, it's still a very competitive price. I have no idea how Sony managed to get it that low, but I have a feeling they'll be losing massive amounts on each system sold.

I don't mean to be argumentative, but being the Nintendo fanboy that I am it is my duty to defend any and all Nintendo related ideas, consoles, and games.

I don't think there's a clear-cut winner here; neither one is going to totally dominate. We'll just have to wait and see how it turns out.

#37295 2 2004-11-21T17:14:33Z tktktk
Very fun, but a bit too easy. On the one hand, jumping and bouncing around while throwing beads all over the place is a blast. Once you get master the controls you can just go crazy. On the other, death is trivially simple to avoid, since you can just sit in a corner and wait for your health to regenerate. Those berry-shooting enemies were very irritating had me doing a lot of that. Plus, it's too easy to reach any area by just holding the up button. I do like the Yoshi's Island style graphics though.

Overall, it's a great little diversion and I definitely recommend it if you want a break from the frustrations of N.

Score: 7/10

Edit: After getting farther into the game, I realized it actually ramps up in difficulty very quickly. It can be frustrating after all. My score still stands though.

Keep in mind, you probably won't be making great models right away. It took me several tries before I was able to make even a simple model. But just try it out, and try to find some of the really great models. In the links section they have the sites from a few incredible constructors that are definitely worth visiting.

#40741 28 2004-12-12T08:07:37Z tktktk
Sorry, but I didn't really like it. Like maximo said in the comments, that kind of bug use is somewhat frowned upon. Also, the upper right room is too hard. It literally took me about thirty tries, respawning right below it. Still, it wasn't too bad, better than your first three anyway.

A few pieces of advice for the future:

1. The most important rule of mapmaking: playtest, playtest, playtest! Make sure every part of your map is both beatable and fun. Even if it is beatable, it may be just too frustratingly difficult for most people, which is not a good thing.

2. Make sure every single item has a purpose. Right down to the last piece of gold, ensure that everything in your map has a reason for being there. If it doesn't need to be there, take it out. It's okay to use gold and whatnot for aesthetic purposes, just in moderation.

3. Ensure that every part of your map goes with the others. In other words, let each part share the theme. For example, this theme could be an enemy type, an interesting style of tileset, or making use of a specific ability. Use this theme throughout the map. You don't have to do this, but most good maps do. And if you can find a concept to base a map on that hasn't been used before, that's all the better.

4. Develop your own unique style. If you look at one of maximo's or LV's maps, you can immediately tell who made it. You can use symmetry, item placement, enemy types, and much more to aid you.

Do NOT give up! Keep trying, I'm sure you'll get it down. If you need any more help, just ask.

#1639 1 2004-12-20T20:11:10Z tktktk
I wrote this story for English class. It's probably the longest story I've written, but it's still fairly short. It's kind of science fictiony I guess, but I didn't think of it that way. Anyway, enjoy!


Living in the Past

The roaring crowd drowned out the grunts and groans of the two fierce competitors. On the brilliantly lit stage, the wrestlers fought, tackling and dodging, each determined to find the others weakness and use it to gain the advantage that he needed to win. It was a close match, but then one of the fighters saw his chance. His opponent was standing with a slight limp. He deftly evaded the approaching adversary, who was attempting to put him in a headlock. The next moment he struck, forcefully pushing the opposing wrestler onto his weaker leg, and slamming him into the ground. He finished the poor, cowering soul off with a quick but devastating body slam. Rick Ralson, the defending champion for nine years running, had once again taken first in the Texas State Wrestling Championship.

I am undefeatable! crowed Rick triumphantly. I will take on anyone, anytime, any

But Ricks giddy, conceited babbling came to a halt, and suddenly he was nowhere to be seen.

* * *

There was no time to lose; the deadline was fast approaching. The blueprints had to be submitted with in a few short hours.

Oh, what am I going to do? whimpered the architect.

He was designing an underground compound for a government operation he wasnt important enough to know about. It had to be both vast and stable, which was something quite difficult given that it was to be two miles beneath the earths surface.

I cant think! said the sickly-looking man. I just cant work under this kind of pressure. They gave me this project because Im Jimmy Wilton, one of the greatest architects alive, but they wouldnt listen when I tried to tell them Im no good at designing structures to take immense pressure. What am I going to do? I cant

He went on like this for several minutes, then sullenly attempted to continue with his work. He scribbled some lines and symbols down on the paper. He stared at the blueprints through his thick glasses, then crumpled them up and began whining again.

Oh, its no use! Ill never be able to do this. Its impossible! He burst into tears, sobbing violently but a moment later all that remained was a small damp spot on the carpeted floor.

* * *

The wind struck at the assassins face with sandy needles, but she gave it no heed. There was only one thing to pay attention to: the target. Nothing else mattered to this cold, emotionless sniper, nothing else existed. Of course, that wasnt entirely true, she had to listen for the slightest noise from her surroundings. The guards were mostly either unconscious or asleep in the surrounding tents to avoid the blistering heat. Still, there was plenty of danger involved, at least enough that the target had to be neutralized within the next few minutes.

The assassin knew little about the unfortunate man who would be dead momentarily, only a few physical characteristics to identify him with. The flap covering the entrance to the tent had been removed. From her spot behind a few conveniently placed crates, she peered inside and instantly recognized her target, who was speaking rapidly in Arabic to a few companions. The killer knew that once the shot had been fired she would have literally seconds to escape from the camp. Annette Kavorsky took a deep breath and readied her rifle. She slowly aimed it at the targets forehead and the gun dropped silently to the sand, alone and useless without its mistress.

* * *

Oh, those memories, whispered the man in the black cloak. Those memories so painful.

He had been there kneeling on the ground for several hours or maybe an eternity recalling events from the distant past. They could not be changed, not without severe consequences, and not by him even if he wanted to. There was only one man who could do that, and he had disappeared long ago.

Why, muttered the man to himself, why cant I just move on? Theres nothing holding me back except

The black-cloaked man stopped. He got up and looked around cautiously. Something something wasnt right. Could it be? Could it possibly be that

But from here his thoughts, along with his existence, faded into nothingness.

* * *

When Jimmy Wilton opened his eyes, which were still red and bleary from his minor breakdown, he saw nothing. There was nothing to see but a pitch white void that seemed to engulf both his body and his mind. Understandably, this caused poor Jimmy to go into a state of panic. His first instinct was to scream, and scream he did, but it came out as a sorry little squeal that was instantly stifled by the immense space. He desperately tried to get ahold of himself, which he did best by using simple logic.

All right, Jimmy reasoned to himself in a voice he could barely hear. There has to be an explanation for this. Maybe Ive died a meteor fell on my office or something and this is where Ive ended up. But this isnt how I would have imagined heaven or hell. Maybe its some kind of purgatory. Or maybe

At this point he trailed off, because he noticed a tiny speck quite a distance away. When he saw it, he was simultaneously compelled to run away from and towards it. Then he realized that he was not floating, as he had previously assumed, but standing on a white surface (or transparent, it was impossible to tell), and he was perfectly capable of walking around.

Maybe Im dreaming, Jimmy said thoughtfully. Yes, that must be it. Well, I suppose I should go and see what that little dot is.

So off he went. The speck never seemed to get any closer, even after he had walked for what seemed like several hours. Finally it began to change shape, first widening, and then becoming three distinct shapes, which he finally decided must be people. They seemed to be coming towards him even as he continued tirelessly toward them. They became more and more detailed, until at last he could make them out easily.

First there was a tall, shirtless man, tanned with rippling muscles. He looked to be about in his mid-twenties, and strode towards him with a confident air. Next was a woman with long black hair dressed from head to toe in beige camouflage. She seemed perfectly calm, as though she was trained to keep her cool in any situation. Finally came what appeared to be a man in a ragged cloak as black as coal, with the rest of his features except for his shadowy face hidden from plain view.

They were approaching quickly now, until finally both Jimmy and the other three stopped, staring for an awkward moment. The shirtless man was the first to speak.

And who might you be? he inquired, almost condescendingly. When he got no immediate response, he said to his two companions, Looks like weve got ourselves a mute one here.

M-My names Jimmy. Jimmy Wilton.

Well, thats more like it. Im Rick, and this heres Annette and um well, he wont tell us his name, so I just call him Josh.

As Rick mentioned him, the black-cloaked man bristled, as though he did not much like his new nickname.

You wouldnt happen to know where we are or why were here, would you? asked Jimmy timidly.

This time it was Annette who spoke. Im sorry, but we dont know whats going on any better th

Actually, I have a good idea of why we have been sent here, interrupted Josh. We have been Moved from our dimension to this one. I believe the man who did this wanted me

WELCOME, the voice emanated from every direction, a deafening and hostile blast of sound. "I AM THE CREATOR OF THIS DIMENSION. I HAVE MOVED THE FOUR OF YOU BECAUSE I HAVE NEED OF ONE OF YOU.

This just gets weirder and weirder, whispered Rick.

IN ORDER TO DETERMINE WHICH OF YOU I NEED, I HAVE DEVISED A SERIES OF TESTS. THEY WILL BEGIN MOMENTARILY, AND WILL CONTINUE UNTIL ONLY ONE OF YOU REMAINS.

Until only one of us remains? cried Jimmy. He began slapping his face violently. Wake up! Wake up! Wake up!

Snap out of it, Jim, said Rick. Well all get through this.

Im not sure about that, replied Josh sadly. That man has complete control over this dimension. He could make a boulder appear over each of our heads and crush us if he wanted to.

How do you know all this? asked Annette. And why did he bring us here?

But before Josh could answer, their surroundings began to change. A leafy ground appeared beneath their feet, slowly becoming more detailed, more real. The whiteness above their heads morphed to a robins egg blue, with a few wispy clouds starting to take shape. Most noticeable, however, was the dense green shrubbery that formed all around them, and in the distance a monstrous volcano was being created, complete with spewing lava.

None of this is real, is it? Jimmy asked, shaken. I mean, we cant be hurt or anything, right?

Of course we can be hurt! snapped Josh. How else do you think he intends to get rid of us, you blasted fool?

Now they were stopped again, this time by an ominous rumbling. Suddenly black smoke and ash mingled with the air, and an instant later fiery liquid death followed, moving down the side of the volcano at an alarming rate. By that time the best course of action had become quite obvious, but Jimmy felt the need to instruct his companions in case they were unsure of what to do.

Run!

The other three had already started off, however, and Jimmy was soon following close behind them. As they looked back, they saw that the area they were standing in only seconds before had gone from a deep green to a bright orangy red. Branches and vines scraped against their legs and obstructed their path. Stones and roots caused stumbling and cost them precious seconds. The going was painfully slow, and each time they looked back the lava had oozed closer, obliterating the foliage they had only just struggled through. It was near enough that they could feel the lavas heat radiating as though already searing them with invisible tendrils. Twenty feet ten feet

Then without warning the four came to a cliff. Hundreds of feet straight down below them was a vast ocean, glistening beautifully, basking in the last rays of a pink and orange sunset. It would have been a lovely and tranquil sight had it not been for the dire situation they were in.

We have to jump, theres no other choice! yelled Annette.

With no time to spare, all four leaped off the edge and into the thin air. Icy wind blasted all around them, and had they looked up they would have glimpsed the molten rock drop off the cliff behind them. However, all they could see was the azure sky and the thick inky indigo of the water below.

ALL FOUR OF YOU HAVE PASSED THE FIRST TEST. THE SAME WILL NOT BE SAID FOR THE NEXT ONE.

And then all at once their surroundings began to change again. As they fell, they saw the ocean below them morph into dry land. The sun was rewound from twilight to early afternoon. The four realized with confusion that the sandy ground was being moved away from them, giving them the odd sensation of falling up, flying from the ground although still hurtling downwards. It finally stopped, and by this time they were a good five miles up and could barely see it at all. To make matters worse, ring-shaped metallic barriers formed before their eyes, each one armed with a deadly blue electric charge that jumped back and forth through their centers. They floated patiently in midair, waiting to zap into oblivion anyone who so much as touched them.

This is crazy! hollered Rick. No one can survive a fall like this. Even if we were to make it past those zappy things, wed still be toast!

Although they were in too much of a panic to realize it, communicating should have been impossible. The dimension keeper had forgotten that with the wind blasting in their ears it would be difficult to hear anything at all, let alone a complete sentence. It was this that saved them.

We can control how we fall, said Josh, if we lean in the direction we want to move in. We can also fall faster or slower depending on our aerodynamics. Steve may well be insane, but he knows what hes doing. There is a way to pass this test.

It was difficult to veer away from the death traps; they had to begin well before they neared one. The first one was easy to avoid; it was a blur as they sped by. However, what lay ahead (or rather, below) was essentially an aerial minefield. The four were split up, each leaning in a different direction to dodge one that they were coming at straight on. They could see the electrical surges coursing through each one of the metallic killers.

There were more and more of them, with narrower gaps between them. They floated, silent and emotionless, as the four flipped frontward and backward in a desperate fight for their lives. Then suddenly there were no more, there was only the ground below them, which was getting nearer all the time.

Well, thats great, we survived those electric barriers, but how the heck are we gonna survive hitting the ground?! asked Jimmy frantically.

It looks as thought well have to use that to slow ourselves down, replied Josh, and the others looked to where he was pointing.

It was a mesa with a sheer rock face on all sides. It curved gradually at the bottom and eventually flattened out and became the ground, basically making the entire thing a gigantic quarterpipe.

Everyone slow yourselves down as much as you can, and try to steer close to the side of the mesa, Josh instructed.

They had gotten used to maneuvering themselves by now, but it was still a difficult task to get near the rock wall. Closer, closer and in an instant the top of the mesa was above them, and they found themselves staring at smooth reddish brown stone, whizzing past about five feet away.

Get as close as you can to it, but dont touch it!

The other three did as they were told, but now the vertical rock became an extremely steep slope.

On my mark, put your feet to the rock and slide, making sure not to push off.

Are you nuts? said Jimmy. This cant possibly

Now! yelled Josh, and there was no time to argue.

The four put their shoes against the slope. Each could feel their rubber soles wearing down. The curve of the slope became less and less steep, but they were still going at a terrific speed.

Lean forward and start running now, or youll fall backwards!

They began running down the slope, which by this time was nearing a forty-five degree angle. Their bodies were strained with the immense pressure of gravity that was pulling them down. As the slope curved into the horizontal ground, it felt as though they were being pulled into the earth itself. They tumbled and rolled across the hot sandy ground, and lay where they had fallen for a good while.

Annette was the first to recover. Is everyone all right? she asked.

Ohhh, groaned Jimmy. We just fell thousands of feet and ran down the side of a cliff. How can we be all right?

Wheres Rick?

The response was a whimper of pain from several yards away. I think I broke my leg, winced Rick.

It could have been much worse for all of us, Josh muttered. That maniac has to be stopped somehow.

How do you know that guy? asked Jimmy. It seems you know exactly why were here, so would you mind explaining?

Hello? Im in pain over here, called Rick through gritted teeth.

Dont interrupt, replied Josh curtly.

But my leg!

It will have to wait, we dont have anything to treat it with anyway. Now, lets see it started back many years ago, in my junior high school. My name was Reginald, but I hated it with a passion and no longer go by it. I was a nerd, or at least I was labeled as such because I was too intelligent and unpopular to be cool. The other kids picked on me constantly. Get out of here, Reginald, theyd jeer, no one likes your style! They werent exactly good at giving insults, but they would practically beat me into the ground if I got in their way, the brutes. I was an outcast, and I hated my life.

Then I met Steve now Dr. Steven Cardgage and he became the only friend I ever had. Now we were outcasts together. He was always dreaming up crazy ideas, and one day he told me that he would to dedicate his life to finding a way to create his own world, where he could be free from social pressure. I went along with it for a little while, but I quickly began to lose interest in his scheme. Steve, on the other hand, became more and more obsessed. Eventually it resulted in the end of our friendship. He pursued his goal, adding on even more crazy notions along the way, like turning back time itself. Eventually he became an accomplished physicist, but a few years ago he disappeared without a trace. Now

SO ALL FOUR OF YOU HAVE SURVIVED ONCE AGAIN. IT DOES NOT MATTER. IN THE NEXT TEST

That is enough! bellowed Josh. You think youve figured out how to control our dimension from this one, eh, Steve? You cant even control things properly in this one. Even I could do better!

ARE YOU ASKING FOR A CHALLENGE?

You bet I am.

All at once the space around them was white again, and a man materialized. He was short, overweight, and generally unimpressive.

You think you can do better, Steve sneered, then go ahead and try.

And Josh was gone. For a few moments they stood in silence, then Steve disappeared as quickly as he had come and Josh was back once more.

Well, that was easy, he said. Steve always did have a problem with making rash decisions. Taking advantage of his pride was a cinch. In case you were wondering, I Moved him to a mental institution, where he belongs. We should be going back ourselves any moment now.

Theres just one thing I still cant figure out, said Jimmy. We still dont know why he needed us here in the first place.

That egomaniac needed someone here to see his triumph, when he would take revenge on society by messing with reality in our dimension. He meant to take only me so that he could rub it in my face that he had finally achieved his dream, but he still hadnt mastered control over time and space, so he took four people rather than just one. Apparently he couldnt actually see us until he materialized, so he tried to weed you three out with his tests, believing only I would be clever enough to get through them.

Well, I guess we wont be seeing each other again, said Annette.

Thats right.

The four had just enough time to say their goodbyes before fading once again out of existence.

* * *

Rick nearly collapsed on his broken leg as fans screamed all around him.

You really are the greatest! shouted one.

He sighed. No, Im not the greatest. Just a guy who happens to be good at wrestling.

* * *

Jimmy uncrumpled the blueprints, and took few deep breaths. He stared calmly at the sketches and diagrams for several minutes. Then he smiled.

Thats it, he said simply, and got to work.

* * *

Annette picked her rifle off the ground. She looked sadly through the tent opening at the man she was to kill. He was talking and laughing.

Maybe some were meant to kill, Annette murmured, but Im not one of them. She got up and slipped cautiously away, leaving her weapon behind.

* * *

Reginald sat in silence, thinking one last time over those painful memories of his past. He gave a deep, heaving sigh.

Those days are over. Time to focus on the ones ahead. With that, he silently walked away, towards the rising sun.

#45628 5 2005-01-12T01:13:21Z tktktk
Yep, each item has its uses, whether originally intended or not. When M/R first made the game, they made the items with the assumption that they would be used the way they were meant to be used. Wrong.

Gold can be used not only to add two seconds to your score, but also to be aesthetically pleasing, for delaying platforms, mines, and launchpads, and to offer extra challenge in custom maps. The same goes for the other items. Do you think it was ever intended for a normal door to be a tiny, insanely-hard-to-jump-on platform? Or for thwumps to be used for a wall of death? Nope.

Let's face it, there really aren't all that many items, and if they were all used only the way they were intended maps would quickly become boring and similar. We adapt them, and use them to make the most of what we have. With gold, you can't exactly use it to help your time, so we used it for other stuff. Make sense?

As far as difficulty, if a map is truly well put together it will be fun for a player of nearly any skill, but it would be impossible to make it that way without a few optional objectives for the veterans.

#1902 1 2005-01-25T22:11:02Z tktktk
First, a disclaimer: I have nothing against those who make DDAs and even enjoy watching their work.

Now, here's my argument in a nutshell:

Quote: tktktk @ Jan 4 2005, 02:06 AM (slightly edited)
I'm seriously wishing DDAs didn't go towards your overall rating. Makron is now in the second place spot, above the likes of LittleViking, Lucidium and stepself . Granted, he has several good regular maps, but main reason he's there is his DDAs.

This has happened numerous times briefly with people specializing in DDAs, but frankly I'm getting sick of it. No offense to makron, wedgie or any others like them, I do enjoy your work, but I feel that DDAs in general are just rated too highly. While the average rating maybe a 3 for regular maps, the DDA average is probably about a 4. The logic people are basing their ratings on is obviously skewed; an average DDA should be a 3.

I for one don't want to see the best mapmakers be forgotten and replaced with a bunch of n00bs who happen to be able to churn out a few nice DDAs.

Who's with me?
If there are people who really want things to stay like they are, perhaps a compromise could be reached, like a button under average rating that says "Including DDAs" or something.

However, I know there are plenty of people here who agree with me. Many of us want the top rated authors list to represent how good people are at making regular, playable maps. I'd like anyone who does to post here.

People that have signed:
  • tktktk
  • maximo

  • Tsukatu

  • HeartView
  • James
  • Triple T
  • Tornado TK
  • syntax
  • Lancer
  • Echarin
  • Slt10T
Test maps have also been suggested to be taken out of the authors average rating, so this petition is for that too now I guess.

Also, LouDog and brickman suggested something that would be very useful and another good alternative:
Quote: brickman, Jan 26 2005, 10:02 PM
Everyone has preferances. Some people don't like to mix thinking with their reflexes, some people dislike survival maps, some people see no point in race maps, etc. Thus, its safe to say that if there was a filter for every category, most of them would be used, even if they weren't all important enough to request individually. When people don't like a type of map, they probably won't play it and thus don't care about how a person does with that type of map as much as they do a category they like. And what if I just want to know who makes, say, the best puzzles *cough*Lucidium*cough*. Filters work there too. Do filters on the all authors, newest and specific author pages; and it'll probably be a long time before we ask for more stuff.

#50450 50 2005-02-15T04:50:25Z tktktk
Hey guys, not to give you an extra deadline, but Mare and Raigan said that we have to have our map suggestions for 1.4 user levels in by the last week of February. I think it'd be really awesome if we could get some of the best entrants into the game, since they would fit well with the other levels. This isn't the contest deadline or anything, but if you want your maps to have a shot at making it in you'd better submit them by then.

And here, I'll start us off:

Map: N Your Eyes
Author: Kablizzy

First off, I could absolutely see this in the main game. There isn't a single item that looks odd or out of place like so many other user maps have. The tileset is very nice, clean and simple. The gold placement was good too.

I sorta liked how the drones were placed as well. Metanet levels often seem to have everything symmetrical except for one or two key elements, and in this case the drones were it. They offered quite a different experience depending on which way you went up... but then again there was no real reason to go right since left is so much faster. The exit switch was an interesting challenge that could be undertaken in several different ways.

Overall the level was nice and easy. It kind of reminiscent of nine's Quick Round series, particularly Technology. Nothing too frustrating either, I really couldn't think of anything bad about it. It was a great way to kick off NC6.

Score: 42


Map: defenscerrator
Author: Eli

Another good attempt as far as Metanetness, just a few little things to pick on. You went slightly overboard on the gold in the upper right and the pieces between the doors in the lower left looked a little weird to me. The upper left looks messy and cluttered, and there wasn't much reason for having three rockets; one or two would have sufficed. On the other hand it does have style, and I liked how the gold in the exit room went alongside the tiles.

The upper right felt kind of monotonous going through that thrice, and those gausses were like attack dogs if you tried for the gold in the upper left (not necessarily a bad thing). The bounce blocks and mines seemed relatively well placed, not LV-caliber but good nonetheless. The last part was my favorite, the way the one-ways were set up with the rockets was unique and the gold was fun to try for.

Overall an above average map with three distinct parts, each with its own feel. The first part was boring, the second so-so, the last excellent.

Score: 35


Map: I Get Around
Author: HeartView

Well barring the slightly out of place circle of tiles in the beginning, this one is a beauty with its graceful, streamlined look.

However, the gameplay itself is where there are a few problems. The bottom part is nicely designed and fun to play. Then you come to the two up-facing thwump areas. The one on the left is simple enough, but the right one has that pesky floorguard that makes it just a little too difficult to try for. I did sorta like how you were forced to use the thwump to get up to the final level. The part that kills the level for me though is the last part with the exit switch. The lazer drone combined with the floorguard is a deadly combination. If you're going to make a part of your level that frustrating and difficult, put it near the beginning.

Overall, this is an average level that's partially ruined by an irritating ending.

Score: 29


Map: Up, up, and... run away!
Author: brickman

Hmm... sorta like Metanet infused with brickman. The sides and top are perfect, but then there's those double sided one-ways and such in the bottom and center that look a little clumsy.

It plays very nicely though. To start you can either just drop through or take the jump onto the first bounce block. Then it's a reasonably simple climb to the switch. After avoiding the rocket, you drop down and can either repeat the process on the other side or risk taking on the guarded exit switch with extra obstacles. If you went ahead with the other switch you can cruise on past the floorguard and, avoiding that annoying little mine, drop into the exit.

Overall, this is a strong level with a well-balanced difficulty, in spite of forcing two very different styles to collide rather awkwardly.

Score: 36

Edit: After a bit of contemplation I decided to spread the scores out slightly to ensure that future maps will be graded on the same scale. Really sorry guys, hope that's okay, and it won't happen again.

#50833 61 2005-02-19T00:45:56Z tktktk
Some more:

Map: Turret Arena
Author: Maniac

Designwise, the only thing that sticks out is the exit. The tiles that enclose it aren't connected which makes it look a little funny. The top half also looks a tad cluttered, but nothing terrible. The general design is kind of uninspired. It also kind of looks more like an extension of your style than Metanet's.

Now, this level is hard. And it's not just that it's hard, it's that it's not much fun to play either. The lower part is fine, the center switch was a nice little diversion, and the entire bottom half is actually kind of easy. But then you get into the top half and it all goes downhill. Two rockets and two gauss turrets in a sea of bounce blocks makes things too difficult. I think it would have been much more balanced if there was only one gauss.

Overall this is a hard and frustrating map with more bad qualities than good. This isn't to discourage difficult maps, but just remember they have to be fun as well.

Score: 24


Map: Moving away, but getting closer
Author: Echarin

A little too random-looking if you ask me. The double one-ways in the center are a no-no, and those chaingun pens are just plain weird. I don't like the way the gold is scattered either. Gold should be placed in hard to reach places, not the easiest path.

The only real threat while playing through the level is the chainguns, which happen to be my least favorite enemy. They tend to result in lots of cheap, unfun deaths, which unfortunately was the case in this level. In spite of all that I did manage to have fun with this level however. There was at least some skill and timing involved avoiding the chainguns, which was good since it stopped it from becoming a game of Russian roulette. The floorguard was useless, but the gauss turrets and most of the mines were used well.

Overall, an okay map made a little more interesting (but not necessarily better) by a couple of chainguns.

Score: 30

Map: Arrow'd!
Author: so_what/nevermore

Sigh... if I were to close my eyes and pick randomly out of the levels on Numa, this is exactly the kind of map I would expect to pick. It just doesn't look or play Metanet. At all. There are numerous little messy things that are characteristic of a regular 'ol user map. There's also that irritating exit/adjacent door glitch.

It plays okay, but again, not like a Metanet level would at all. The first section is your standard drivel. The lazer drones presented a considerable challenge, but the chaingun wasn't a threat at all. The switches behind the gauss turrets were pretty simple, as was the exit switch room. Dropping to the goal was very easy if you went about it the right way. The level was somewhat fun, but it didn't have anything I hadn't seen before.

Overall this was a pretty simple map with one or two nice moments and several rather dull ones, with virtually no Metanetness whatsoever.

Score: 25


Map: Tombs of Giza
Author: so_what/nevermore

This one has a nice design. The lower left could have used a one-way rather than two doors, and the exit shouldn't have been half covered like that, but otherwise good job. I really could see this as a main game level.

The first part of the map is very easy, and almost becomes a chore as you continue to play through. The bottom left section is good; the gauss turret is challenging to get past and the thwumps are easy with the right strategy. Then there's the rocket area, the most difficult part. That top switch is a real pain to get, and requires a lot of skill and strategy.

Overall this is a solid level with three sections, ranging from dully simple to satisfyingly difficult.

Score: 35

#52000 87 2005-02-28T01:37:35Z tktktk
All right, you asked for 'em:

Map: Fluidity
Author: Lancer

Okay, like you said in the description, this would definitely be in the Freestyle category if there was such a thing. It's very reminiscent of 0-0 in its design, and aside from those four pieces of gold that are too close to the tiles it could easily pass for an earlier level. It's a large sprawling level that has a good style to it.

The level is quite fun to play, and it's very open to different routes. It's really simple to complete, and even to all-gold. I don't know why, but it was very frustrating when I tried to though. In my opinion it could have used something to get up more easily on the right side; rockets and sheer walls tend not to mix well. Other than that the level flows very smoothly. The center part with the gauss turret is nice and seems to be the heart of the level. However, most of the top area feels bland and unexciting while at the same time somehow still fun.

Overall, a very simple map similar to some of the earliest levels, with a nice flow but some rather boring parts.

Score: 37


Map: Tension
Author: Lancer

Woah. Couldn't be more different from Fluidity, and that's not really a good thing. There are several things in here that, while creative, Metanet just wouldn't do. The biggest one is the bottom right. Not only does it seem rather cluttered, but there's no way I'd ever see something like this in the main game, with the one-way clusters and all that. The left looks ever-so-slightly mine happy, but overall okay.

Hard, and overly long too. The beginning is probably the best, especially the bottom bit with the drones. Getting back up while avoiding the gauss is annoying and I kept dying there for some reason. The lazer area is very complex, and the one-ways are like cages of death if you're not careful. The exit switch is one of the few areas that displays some elegant simple fun. Then there's the exit section, at first I didn't realize that the best way to get up there is to jump to the little slanted tile first.

Overall this is a lengthy, difficult and somewhat frustrating map that bears little resemblance to a Metanet level but still has some redeeming qualities.

Score: 29


Map: Angularity
Author: JeR(K)

You've got to be kidding. Why do you guys submit stuff like this that you've got to know has nothing to do with the theme? The "forcefield" of locked doors around the switch, the gold on top of the switch surrounded by the messy mine room, and the ridiculously cluttered bottom section make it obvious that this is a user map, and a subpar one at that.

This is one looooong level, and there is very little enjoyment to be had in playing it. The center drone part is very slow, and then you drop into the difficult and claustrophobic gauss room. You often have to sit waiting for the lazer drone to move out of the line of sight. Then there's the mine-laced room that's very easy and just seems like another obstacle to get through. By this time I've pretty much lost track of all the switches you have to waste your time getting before sliding into the exit.

Overall, this is a very long and tedious map that is not in any way enjoyable to play through.

Score: 19


Map: Inversion
Author: maximo

Wow. The only real thing I can pick on is that it actually feels too polished to be a main game level. Still, the elegant simplicity makes up for the overly refined style, and I can see Mare and Raigan making something like this. The layout sort of reminds me of 39-2 but it doesn't play anything like it.

I like how the difficulty ramps up slowly as you move higher up in the level. It starts with a simple floorguard, then goes to 2 floorguards and a gauss, then the floorguards and a rocket, and finally the two gausses and floorguards at the top. The drones are a nice touch and balance out the level. The action is fast paced and extremely fun. The difficulty is perfect, it's a great challenge for beginners and a quaint little romp for veterans. One of the few things I don't like is how the launchpads are placed so that you can't reach the second side platform at all, or the the second middle platform without difficulty.

Overall I think this is a favorite to win this contest, simple yet elaborate, exciting and fun.

Score: 43

#52598 5 2005-03-05T00:28:57Z tktktk
Here are mine, nothing real special:

+ Rockets. I love rockets, and if you can implement them in a way that doesn't feel overused I will love your map too.
+ Overall polish. This is basically my first impression. Everything should look neat and organized.
+ Symmetry. Not just for symmetry's sake, but in a way that both looks good and helps the gameplay.
+ Color variety. Blue from drones, red from mines, and yellow from gold make a level look visually pleasing.
+ Stylized. The kind of map that you can look at and play without knowing the author and say, "Oh yeah, so and so made this one."
+ Gold. Maps just tend to look empty without it, and it gives you an extra challenge.

- Rockets. Yes, this is sort of a contradiction, but there are sooo many rocket maps out there, and if yours doesn't do anything new with 'em it's just another map among hundreds of others.
- Bugs. I really don't like them, unless they're used in just the right way.
- Unnecessary items. My biggest pet peeve, if there's a single mine or one-way that doesn't need to be there and isn't for aesthetic purposes, I hate it with a passion.
- Frustrating areas. I know, nobody likes them, but for me they can ruin the entire map in some cases.
- Chainguns. Eew. My least favorite enemy, unless you can use them in a way in which they don't result in cheap deaths.

Map: Shelter
Author: stepself

Really cool tileset, unique and clean-looking. The only thing my nitpicking radar picked up was those pieces of gold that were too close to the launchpad. Oh, and the gauss rooms are the only two things that aren't symmetrical, which sort of make it look off balance.

Plays pretty well, very easy if you don't go for gold. It's fun just shooting through those little rooms, but you don't really get to experience any resistance. It's slightly awkward getting from the rocket areas into the chaingun room, but nothing too challenging. As for getting the gold, that's much more difficult. The gold right behind the rocket and in the chaingun room are the hard parts. It took a while to figure out how to get those pieces consistently.

Overall, this is a nice, unique map with only a couple of problems worth mentioning.

Score: 39


Map: Pulvonary
Author: stepself

It's pretty obvious that this was inspired by 25-0, but I have to admit I somewhat prefer the simplicity of the original, at least designwise. I'm not really sure what's up with that asymmetrical gold at the bottom, but I'll go with it. Everything seems pretty well laid out.

It's surprisingly fun just running around the two big loops Sonic-style, and the gauss turrets really aren't a threat as you're doing so. In fact, none of the enemies are very threatening provided you don't do anything stupid. Surprisingly the all-gold isn't too hard either. It's a fun level though and that's the important thing. I do NOT, however, like that bounce block membrane, because that's the only part when I actually do tend to make stupid mistakes.

Overall, an easy level with fun fast-paced side areas and a somewhat annoying ending.

Score: 37


Map: Generation N
Author: chimneysweep

Eeeeeeew. Okay, I'll admit that, amazingly enough, there aren't any major problems. It's just ugly. Really ugly. The closest thing I've seen to this in style is probably 8-1, but it looked and played way better.

The biggest problem with the gameplay are the massive shortcuts. Although you said that "lesser players miss the easier routes", anyone who's not ignorant or blind will be able to spot them with ease. It's actually hard not to take a shortcut. The first part of the level was easy and mildly enjoyable. Then there's the thwump that seems to just be chillin' in the middle of nowhere, and it's off to get that first switch. And then from there everything seems random and confusing, and eventually you just sort of wander bewilderedly to the exit.

Overall, this map consists of a series of seemingly random rooms and corridors riddled with shortcuts.

Score: 21

Map: N Ultra 64
Author: Daddaluma

Nice nice. I like the jagged edges. What's with the drones on that invisible path though? Not good. That aside, the map's a beauty, nice clean and spacious.

The trapdoors aren't a necessity, but they sure make things easier. Then you can use the bounce blocks or the side walls to get up. Only one side switch is required, then the middle one guarded by the drones. Then you can finally enter the center area, get the switch, and drop to the exit. I like the upper bounce blocks and how you can just barely access them from the center area. The side walls are nice too; there's something satisfying about climbing them as they jut out above you. The level is pitifully easy, and would for the most part work well among later first column levels.

Overall a simple, open level that is good for beginners or a quick play for veterans.

Score: 36

#53288 39 2005-03-08T23:53:23Z tktktk
Quote: Daddaluma, Mar 8 2005, 06:50 AM
@tktktk: I really have no idea what you have against the teleports being in the real game. It takes away nothing from the gameplay and adds in a little bit of cool style.

It's not teleporters specifically, but bugs in general. But here's why I'm definitely against teleporters:

1. There's no way to distinguish between them and regular launchpads.

2. Virtually any map that has one lacks the polish we're looking for anyway.

3. It's inconsistent with the other levels. It might be cool, but if you start out with your basic items for the first 300 maps and then add these just out of the blue, you're going to leave people very confused.

I don't mind things like squeezing through tight spaces or trapped drones quite as much, and I think Lucidium's Easy Squeezy and LV's One-Way are some rare examples of bugs used in great maps with the right kind of feel to them.

Map: Simplistic Confusion
Author: makron

Okay maximo, I know it's you. Stop pretending and come clean. No, but really, this looks so much like one of maximo's simpler maps, and that's a good thing. It there's not one thing wrong with the design, and everything's laid out perfectly.

Easy, easy, easy, fun. Seriously, I can beat this about nine times out of ten, and even enjoy doing so each time. Now, getting the gold, ohhhh is that a different story. It took me 45 minutes to all-gold this. No kidding. I don't know why, it just did. I often talk about enemies not being a threat. When I tried for the gold those two gausses became some of the most threatening and competent enemies I've ever seen, almost to the point of being cheap. Now the ending is the best part for me. It's the easiest part, but somehow it's just uber-fun.

Overall, a really fun map with somewhat cheap enemies if you try for the gold.

Score: 40


Map: Sudden Diversion
Author: makron

Nice again. A place for everything and everything in its place. You could really tell that everything was meant to be that way and there wasn't much you could improve on it.

I liked the difficulty a little more on this one. Harder to complete and easier to all-gold than SC. The main ways I died were when I was going into the rocket room and getting the exit switch. The former was the only frustrating part of the map. The exit switch was creatively placed so that you had to either stand on or walljump off the thwumps. All the enemies seem to be placed almost scientifically to achieve their desired effect.

Overall, a nice short level with well-placed items and good difficulty.

Score: 40


Map: Platforms
Author: Heartview

Humdeedum... let's see here... gauss turrets touching the walls?! Nooooooooo*dies* Ahem. Now, there are several main game levels with no gold at all, but I don't think this level looks right without any. Just too plain.

Seems too much like a "fetch quest" to me. It's a reasonably simple map, but most of the difficulty comes from getting a switch from each of the very similar platforms. You do virtually the same thing for each switch, and while I wouldn't mind it for three or four, you're stuck running around on a wild goose chase for ten of them. It's a good thing you had those spaces between mines for walljumping, or I would have been tearing my hair out trying to get up all those platforms. That said, the experience somehow wasn't that bad. It was somewhat enjoyable, at least until you start to tire of the repitition.

Overall, a somewhat fun level that suffers from severe monotony and repetition.

Score: 27


Map: Amun's Revenge
Author: Kablizzy

Please, tell me what you did to make this. Did you work on it jointly with Mare and Raigan or something? It's amazing. You've outmetanetted Metanet. My hat's off to you. Now there's just one small problem with the interface: the switch in the last room. What purpose does it serve? I just stared at it and stared at it and could not figure out why you put it there.

The map plays beautifully for the majority of the time. The first part does get tedious after multiple retries. The first floorguard was easy, the second was a little tougher unless you went 'round back. I liked how you could choose how you took the exit switch. The climb to the exit was definitely the hardest part. I could avoid the lazers easily enough, but that gauss was surprisingly merciless. I loved how the gold was placed in the level, it really helps the map as a whole.

Overall, a great, very Metanet map that had a slight difficulty issue and an oddly-placed switch.

Score: 41

Triple wall jump

#56217 139 2005-03-26T19:53:26Z tktktk
Wow, judging is going pretty slowly. Here you guys go:

Map: Fiesta
Author: LouDog004

Similar to stag tight and stalag might, only on a grid and with lazer drones. Nothing to really complain about, except that the mines seem to be placed pretty much at random.

A cakewalk if you just go for the exit, but nearly impossible if you go for gold. There's not much incentive to go through the heart of the map; in fact you're encouraged to just move along the outskirts. The lazer drones can be a threat when you least expect them, firing their shots from across the whole map. I didn't feel like there was a whole lot of effort put into this. There's nothing wrong with it, but there's really nothing that makes you actually want to play it.

Overall, an easy map with somewhat cheap enemies and not too much reason to really like it.

Score: 28


Map: Adding
Author: Ande

Nice indeed. The tileset really reminds me a lot of Lucidium's Jacks, albeit less eye-catching. It's seems odd to me that you would put a bounce block in a relatively cramped space and then leave the space in the upper right blank. Also there's that recessed part in the upper right that lacks gold, which looks kind of inconsistent.

Plays nicely, nothing special but solid and fun. At times it seems a little hard to get around for some reason, but most of the time it flows very well. The gauss turrets are well placed and balance the difficulty perfectly for both completion and all-gold. It didn't really stand out as a map I'd pick out of a bunch of great ones to play, but like I said, solid and fun.

Overall a balanced and no-nonsense map that shows some good thought in most places, with one or two exceptions.

Score: 38


Map: omgz get teh thing!!1
Author: Tsukatu

Tsk, tsk. Gold on switches, gold on doors, and an embedded thwump. They may not seem like much, but they're enough to tip anyone off that this isn't a Metanet level. Aside from those things it looks fine but personally I think you went a bit overboard with the gold on the bounce blocks.

I didn't care for most of the map. The bottom was nice but forgettable. Only one side switch is needed to get both gold caches, which I didn't mind. The top part was rather pointless; it was easy but still time consuming. Interestingly my favorite parts were getting to the upper level and then dropping smoothly into the goal at the end.

Overall, this is a slightly subpar map with a few design problems, some boring parts and some more interesting ones.

Score: 27


Map: coulomb
Author: newt

Well I'll say this much, that tileset is beautiful. The only thing that stuck out like a sore thumb to me was those two trapdoors (or more specifically the switches). There were a bunch of regular switches and then the trapdoor switches sort of broke the pattern.

Unfortunately gameplay was a little on the weak side. The outside switches were relatively easy to get. The hard part came when I was forced to dodge rockets while waiting for an opening in the drones to get into the hexagons. Even when I got in safely sometimes the rocket would follow me in. Now that I think of it, I don't think the rockets fit in very well with this level, although there's no enemy that could very well replace them.

Overall, a beautiful map to look at with not too much fun factor involved.

Score: 32


Map: Pleh
Author: Echarin

Wow. Amazingly enough not a single complaint-- oh wait, I found one! There's only one mine in the whole dang thing. It's as though you were going to put mines by all the gold and then thought Aw, screw it but forgot to delete that one or something.

The map is obviously unoriginal seeing as it's based off of plue, but at least it's a good clone. Most of the map flows really well. The right part was only so-so for me, but the left two-thirds was great. I liked the bottom room a lot, and how there were two ways to get out, neither being the way you would think of naturally. Also dropping from the top of the level to the bottom had a stupid sense of enjoyment to it. Good difficulty as well.

Overall a great map with some good excitement although done in an overused style.

Score: 38


Map: Alternate
Author: Kablizzy

No real problems here. The only thing to pick on is that the exit switch on top of the exit is a little un-Metanet. Everything else is perfect, nicely balanced and everything.

The starting thwump is completely harmless, and getting in and out of the drone area is easy enough if you're careful. My main concern is the bulk of the level, which consists of doing basically the same thing four times in the floorguard rooms. I don't mind some repitition, but I hate it when I'm forced to get every switch the same way. Most of the challenge of the level is a result of the length, and that's not really a good thing.

Overall, this is an average map, slightly lengthy with a lot of repetitive parts.

Score: 33


Map: chambers net(net)ine
Author: Eli

Just flat out ugly. The only thing actually wrong was some randomly placed gold by the gauss and some in the walls, but it didn't look and feel right to me at all. I also dislike excessive use of multiple doors, but it's okay I guess. The map just has "user map" written all over it though.

It was fun. It really shouldn't have been, but it was. I played for a while without getting too bored or frustrated. It wasn't at all unique or remarkable, it was just good for a little enjoyment. There were too many switches to get I think, and it took a little too long to get them, but nothing terrible. It felt like it could have used some more time to develop into something great.

Overall a fun but very unpolished map that doesn't acheive greatness or instill hatred and disgust.

Score: 31


Map: Math
Author: Ande

Good, no complaints, nothing special. Math is good. Yup. Nothing else to say.

Could have used one or two less drones in my opinion. They always get in your face when you're busy dealing with the rockets and gauss turrets. The exit switch was the hardest for me to get, because the drones like to congregate down there and it's sometimes difficult to get back out. The difficulty was good, and I expect all-golding would be a reasonable challenge. I sort of liked how you can choose which way you wanna get into the exit.

Overall, this was above average with a few minor problems that don't take too much away from the overall enjoyment.

Score: 37

#59707 41 2005-04-12T00:36:10Z tktktk
These are my pointers that I made a while back:

1. The most important rule of mapmaking: playtest, playtest, playtest! Make sure every part of your map is both beatable and fun. Even if it is beatable, it may be too easy or just too frustratingly difficult for most people, which is not a good thing.

2. Make sure every single item has a purpose. Right down to the last piece of gold, ensure that everything in your map has a reason for being there. If it doesn't need to be there, take it out. It's okay to use gold and whatnot for aesthetic purposes, just in moderation.

3. Ensure that every part of your map goes with the others. In other words, let each part share the theme. For example, this theme could be an enemy type, an interesting style of tileset, or making use of a specific ability. Use this theme throughout the map. You don't have to do this, but most good maps do. And if you can find a concept to base a map on that hasn't been used before, that's all the better.

4. Develop your own unique style. If you look at one of maximo's or LV's maps, you can immediately tell who made it. You can use symmetry, item placement, enemy types, and much more to aid you.

And finally... do NOT give up! And if you need more help, just ask.

#61717 221 2005-04-24T02:15:12Z tktktk
Map: Rabbot
Author: LouDog004

Of course this is Metanetty, it's almost certainly based off 19-4. It's nice, the floorguard is a little weird though. It's clean and open too.

Too many enemies. This was a world of frustration for me, and I think the removal of the two corner rockets would really help the difficulty. The drones combined with the rockets were a surefire way to die if it wasn't timed perfectly. I really did not enjoy playing this map. Still, I could tell it was well-made and I just feel like I shouldn't rate it down out of my emotions.

Overall, a level sure to make you scream in frustration, but is well-made and gives a big sense of accomplishment when finished.

Score: 31


Map: Wrenches
Author: maximo

Unique, but this is maximo style and nothing else. The good news is that it carries the polish evident in all his maps, but as with Inversion it's actually too perfect in design.

The concept was creative, but I felt that it would have been more fun without the annoyingly timed drones. I also didn't like the way we were forced to go round and round in laps. The last gripe I have is how difficult it is to get on the thwumps. If the slope had been more gradual it would have been easier and more intuitive. Still, it was a lot of fun to play, and I've never played anything like it.

Overall, a map not very suited to the theme and with a few gameplay problems but still quite good.

Score: 39


Map: eightriggers
Author: rrrobyp

Very good, very good. I could easily see this in the game, the tileset is suited to it perfectly. Nice use of rotational symmetry as well.

It was great, except for the upper right portion of the center area. That was just a little bit too overwhelming, and I ended up dying there much more than anywhere else. The difficulty is good other than that. I liked the laser and chaingun drones the best; although very simple it just felt good.

Overall a well-made map that shows off visually and in playing it.

Score: 38

Map: Around the World
Author: HeartView

There is nothing wrong with this. It's not perfect by any means, but there's nothing wrong with it.

I have to admit I was really dreading the center drone room, but it wasn't as bad as I expected. In fact it was surprisingly simple as long as you got the timing right. A bit of tedium was involved in getting a couple of the switches, but nothing horrendous. The rockets felt good, never frustrating at all.

Overall, this was surprisingly good, and the more I think about it the more I think this deserves a good score.

Score: 40


Map: serrated
Author: newt

Too much gold on the outskirts and it looks ugly in the walls. That about sums it up.

This level reminds me of the shortcomings 47-1 has, only infinitely more so. How you managed to make it so ridiculously hard with only one gauss turret is beyond me. And then the gold. In a Metanet level the concept of all gold is at least conceivable. But here... well, I'd gladly all gold 12-3 rather than this. The hardest thing about this is the limited movement. You can move okay on the bounce blocks, but getting around on any part of the tiles is a chore. Then finally there's the frustration of being stuck in one of the recesses while the gauss gets a free shot at you.

Overall, overly difficult and not fun to play at all due to limited movement and the length of the map.

Score: 22


Map: No gold, no glamour
Author: Echarin

Refreshing. I liked the way this was laid out, with the gold to strive for in the top half of the map and wide open spaces to roam.

I liked this because it was easy to beat and easy but not a pushover to all gold. Just the way it should be. Completion was pretty straightforward. The fun came with the gold, starting with the slightly tedious switches but picking back up walljumping through the column. The gold at the top was easy to reach - five walljumps - but it was fun every time. The side gold was nice too.

Overall good and easy.

Score: 40


Map: Arid Artifact
Author: Maniac

Arid is right. It's so empty... no gold or mines or drones to give it color. The tileset is believable, but the rest just looks like Maniac style. Plus there were some odd asymmetrical doors on the bottom.

I've always disliked it when maps derive their difficulty from sheer length or number of switches. If the map had been half as long I probably would have loved it, with all the action. The enemies were placed such that I could avoid them and have fun doing it, but the with so many enemies and so many switches, eventual death was almost inevitable.

Overall, a lengthy difficult that's bland visually but fun until you finally die.

Score: 33


Map: pulsar
Author: newt

I love the tileset, and the gold in the tiles actually works well and looks good. The launchpad somewhat puzzled me though.

Much too cluttered and crazy in the getting the switches. The laser drones pin you down and the zappies do the rest. I like the outside gold areas a lot, they're the most fun part of the level. I can't think of anything else to say.

Overall an average map with a feeling of claustrophobia and some fun areas.

Score: 34

Map: Sanctuary Revealed
Author: makron

Map: Who is Sam?
Author: Daddaluma

Quite brilliant, reminiscent of the first half of the 50's column.

I liked the flow and symmetry of the two structures on the right of the map. The drone timing seemed a little off though. Another cool thing was how you could choose between going over or through the "M" to get to the exit switch. Very well made map, surprised me a great deal.

Score: 41


Map: Crosswire
Author: sweep

The tileset is beautiful, and works perfectly with the theme.

The bottom gold stresses repetition, not exactly one of the better aspects of gameplay. Another problem is that the side walls are the easiest way to get up to the switch, which means you miss playing the best part of the level. Still, very fun and surprisingly challenging if you choose to go up the center.

Score: 38


Map: Day Tripping
Author: sweep

Nice, but a few little things irk me, like the gold overlapping the bounce blocks.

The thwumps are placed in positions that really make them a nuisance. I sometimes forgot they were there until they politely reminded me with a face full of electricity. Also, I don't know if this was intentional but you can cheat the one-ways in the drone room very easily. It was still fun, but not overly.

Score: 34

#4026 1 2005-08-13T18:54:04Z tktktk
You guys may have heard some say that eventually we're going to run out of ideas for making maps, since there are only so many working combinations of enemies, objects and tiles. I started this project to prove them wrong.

How am I doing this? By making a series of unique maps using only mines, gold, tiles, ninja, and exit. This will show that if I can make fun, challenging, and radically differing maps with such limited resources, we can make exponentially more with all the options available to us. You may have seen the episode I posted on Numa and in the Episodes Thread. That was the first episode in this series. For those of you that didn't see those maps, I encourage you to check them out as well.

My Simple Challenges were limiting in that they each pinpointed one specific aspect of playing N. With these episodes I'll be able to go beyond that limitation and do anything that's conceivably possible with what I have to work with. Also, note that while the Simple Challenges didn't really take advantage of my mapmaking ability, these maps will. Rather than churning these out in large numbers, I'm spending as much time and effort on these as I would any other map.

Here are all the Minimalist Series episodes. I really want feedback on these, so please leave comments, suggestions, etc.
Attachment: post-10-1133029485.txt

Maximo - Float Park

Appearance: 4 points
I liked the symmetry, but a little bland.

Lag/load time: 5 points
Just peachy.

Ease of use: 8 points
Almost anyone can pull off many of the tricks, like the thwump stuff.

Fun factor: 16 points
Bounceblocks and rockets are pretty much always fun.

Ninja rating: 3 points

Overall thoughts: 8 points
Great for cool runs or just to play around on.

Total: 79 points

Basically he's a lawyer on a crusade against violence in video games. That doesn't seem so bad in itself, but the catch is that he's completely and undeniably insane. What you see here isn't all, not by a long shot. The amazing thing is he does something moronic virtually every day.

Exhibit A
Summary: Scott, the author of the video game webcomic VG Cats, receives an email from Jack Thompson claiming that one of Scott's comics is based on false information. Scott informs Jack of his little friend satire. After this point Jack decides to resort to name-calling and threats, and later denies that he even initiated the conversation. Then, like any self-respecting crazed lawyer, Jack tells Scott that if he doesn't stop emailing him he will take legal action.

Exhibit B
Summary: This'll be a little hard to follow, but here goes. Jack, for reasons beyond human comprehension, announces he will donate $10,000 to charity if a game developer will make a game in which a child goes on a mass murder rampage (or something of to that effect) as a result of playing video games. Several of these games pop up, but then Jack withdraws his proposal, announcing he was "only kidding". Apparently he was also kidding about giving money to needy families. The good folks over at Penny Arcade, another video game webcomic, decide they'll be so kind as to donate the $10,000 dollars for him. Jack then proceeds to try and get them arrested.

A quote from one of the guys at Penny Arcade: "Jack actually just called and screamed at me for a couple minutes," Krahulik said. "He said if I email him again I will 'regret it'. What a violent man." Ironic, isn't it?

Here is an editorial that pretty much sums up exactly what needs to be said about this guy, and pretty much runs his feeble and twisted logic into the ground.

The thwump launchers were fairly original and were certainly the most important part of the map. It's not exactly something you can help, but having to go down the little chutes after each jump kind of messes with the seamlessness. When it comes down to it, each jump consisted of being launched and jumping off one wall. I understand that the number of things you can do with that is limited, but I would have liked to have seen a little more variety.

Map Quality: 36 out of 50
I'll be blunt. I hate the map aesthetically because it's messy-looking and lacks gold. That factors in a little bit here. The thwump launching was really fun, once you actually got the hang of it. In the first column with the launchpads in it the diagonal one often slammed me into the ground, which was frustrating. The third column was my favorite; I loved how you sort of bounce off that corner. All in all not a bad map.

Total score: 74


Map: X-rays
Author: Lucidium

Object Use: 43 out of 50
This map makes fantastic and completely original use of a little-known laser glitch. It's obvious that the map is centered around this concept. I definitely would have liked to have seen some more variation in the gameplay, and have the lasers come into play in more ways than were displayed here.

Map Quality: 30 out of 50
Unfortunately, it played rather poorly. The lasers fired completely at random, which was both a blessing and a curse. They kept you on your toes, but many times you would be faced with a near-impossible situation, making things quite frustrating. Fortunately the map was short enough that it wasn't extremely annoying, but any time it's possible to die by chance the gameplay takes a major hit.

Total Score: 73
#112028 135 2005-11-03T06:20:45Z tktktk
Map: Bouncy Bouncy!
Author: Hellheart

Object Use: 24 out of 50
The launchpad oddity theme is somewhat overused, and not particularly impressive. I sort of liked the part where you launch into the trap door, but that was really the most creative use. It felt more like you alternated between launchpad sections and regular action sections rather than having the whole map based on your theme.

Map Quality: 20 out of 50
The map quite simply was not fun to play. It was long, it was difficult, it was cluttered, and often times it was confusing. I had to watch your demo several times to figure out what to do for one area. The rockets suffered from "bad timing syndrome", which caused death on many occasions. All of these things combined made for a map that was quite the opposite of enjoyable.

Total score: 45


Map: Dim-N-Tia
Author: Hellheart

Object Use: 26 out of 50
We've certainly seen this all before, although you made decent use of the concept. The map was definitely focused on what it set out to accomplish, but the route was very convoluted and confusing. The jungle of doors and pseudodoors made it difficult to know where you were supposed to go next.

Map Quality: 23 out of 50
The main problem here was simply how easy it was to finish the level with a simple shortcut. The whole time I was playing through what I think was the intended route, I was thinking "But couldn't I just go that way?" Add to this the general bewilderment of the level, and it just became a maze that was all to easy to circumvent.

Score: 49


Map: Hunter
Author: Brickman

Object use: 27 out of 50
This is quite a common theme, but fortunately it was used pretty well here. Nothing special by any means, but I liked that it consisted mainly of open spaces. I really dislike maps like this when they have narrow twisting corridors, and thankfully this stayed away from that.

Map Quality: 33 out of 50
The map is pretty bare-bones, and I could have done without the DDA-like launchpads. The hardest part of the map was the very end, which is definitely a bad thing. However, the few items that were there were well-placed, and I inexplicably had fun after doing the same things repeatedly. That's gotta count for something.

Score: 60

Map: Flaccid
Author: HeartView

Object use: 31 out of 50
Er... *cough*... you used thwumps. Lots of them. It's a kind of crazy thwump puzzle, but the only real unusual use of them would be the thwump cannon, and you specifically discouraged using that. Still, Mare and Raigan probably wouldn't have imagined something like this...

Map quality: 32 out of 50
This was very difficult, and the intended path wasn't at all apparent. One big thing was that thwump-cannoning seemed to me to be the easiest way up there, allowing you to bypass most of the map. Hellheart's amazing demo saved you in a way though; without it I wouldn't have had the faintest idea of what to do. Stringing together different types of thwump movement felt kind of cool, and kept the map from getting too frustrating.

Total Score: 63


Map: Jantai
Author: Sweep

Object use: 32 out of 50
All right, another KRA, but this one is particularly well-designed. All the elements of the map are clearly made to further the rocket-preserving experience.

Map quality: 40 out of 50
*Vomits at the sight of the clutter* Ew. Okay, anyway, this actually may have been the best map of its kind I've ever played. The best part of it was the rounded walls, because once I learned to use them to my advantage I found it easier and more fun to plan my moves. The bounce blocks worked well too, since you could move around on them to adjust the position of the rocket.

Total Score: 72


Map: Shot Down
Author: nevermore

Object use: 34 out of 50
Very different, and very cool. Two problems with it, though. First, the map is not centered around it although it's used several times. Second, it's easy to die by being smashed into the locked doors. Once you learn to get around that though (it's all in the timing), you can start to enjoy it.

Map quality: 39 out of 50
This is a very fun map that plays quite normally aside from the UOU. That first gauss nearly drove me insane though. My favorite part was the upper area with the thwumps; it felt very professional. Overall the map plays like your basic above-average action level.

Total Score: 73


Map: I like Datarock.
Author: MOLONEY

Object use: 23 out of 50
Decent puzzle, based on a thwump. However, not in any way original. You used it in two ways: a walljumping tool and a "timer". It works fine, but it's nothing special at all. Not everything is based around the thwump, either; you can just go up the side walls to get the exit switch.

Map quality: 27 out of 50
Nothing out of the ordinary here. I didn't really like the switch hidden behind the exit, it's kind of a cheap thing to do. The timer function of the thwump was probably my favorite part, but I've seen the same concept executed much in a much better fashion (see stepself's thwump puzzlers). Overall it was bland, but lacked any real problems.

Total score: 50


Map: Ducking Under
Author: euphoria

Object use: 30 out of 50
I don't think I've seen cheating death used quite in this manner, but obviously the concept isn't new. The drone concept was decent, but it kind of bugs me that you die if you jump into the downward launchpad or move while a drone is on you. Plus, you can squeeze by the thwump even without the launchpad.

Map quality: 22 out of 50
Lots and lots of waiting does not equate to fun. The slow crawl of the drones made it all the more frustrating when a slight misjudgment led to death. That, combined with finding out the aforementioned annoyances, made the map as a whole more an exercise in irritation than anything.

Total score: 52


Map: Industrial Age
Author: euphoria

Object use: 29 out of 50
I don't think this has been done before, although it's not particularly exciting. It may be the focus of the map, but it's really just doing the same thing five times.

Map quality: 22 out of 50
All this did was give me a headache. The drone was a decent touch and broke up the monotony a bit. It seemed unresponsive for some reason, but I guess you can't be faulted for that. As dc443 put it, "I either smack myself dead or don't hit the switch." Not my idea of fun.

Total score: 51


Map: Piano Keys
Author: euphoria

Object use: 36 out of 50
I like it. Very nice use of the thwumps to create a sort of shaky wall. Original and cool, although it would have been nice to see it used in more than just one way.

Map quality: 35 out of 50
Scaling the walls require a good amount of timing. If you don't jump at the right time you'll tend to move slowly downward rather than up. The gold's kinda fun to get, too. That one mine became a very slight problem; I jumped into it once without doing anything out of the ordinary.

Total score: 71


Map: Tight fit
Author: Brickman

Object use: 34 out of 50
Of course, we've all seen a ton of iterations of the the squeeze level. However, this one stands out a little more because of the not-completely-stale concepts involved. No problems with it, either.

Map quality: 36 out of 50
Quite fun. There wasn't any frustration factor, and that helped a lot. I liked the use of launch pads to help squeeze through some sections. The part with the first one way was kind of cool and different. The map didn't offer up much of a challenge, but maybe that wasn't a bad thing.

Total score: 70


Map: I Am Your Father
Author: sweep

Object use: 47 out of 50
Absolutely friggin' brilliant. I've never seen anything like it, and the concept is downright revolutionary. I think the idea is realized as well as it's physically possible for it to be; the launchpad system is as good as one can reasonably expect.

Map quality: 40 out of 50
This map is very enjoyable to play. The control scheme is confusing (although there's no way around that), but once you get used to it you basically have full control over the movement of the rocket. Mind you, it's extremely hard to control, but you still have complete control over it. In my mind this is the clear cut winner so far.

Total score: 87

Map: The Rage of Innocence
Author: SOLARION

I'm fairly certain I've seen everything in this map before. The trapped drones were the least common, but they're really just big mines anyway. The map wasn't focused on any unusual object use, either; it was broken up a bunch of other little rooms.

Map: Thwump Ramage 1

Map quality: 35 out of 50
