I still think it wouldn't be right for votes to have been shown for HOF. I think it's different for awards, because there's a singular winner... but when there's several, I think a list works better.

Quote: tktktk
I think your main point is that there are a bunch of winners, and they should be honored equally. #163813 35 2006-04-11T06:46:16Z tktktk
You guys are churning out maps faster than I have time to play them. I haven't had enough time to give comments on all of them yet, let alone make too many maps of my own. Some of these might be outdated if changes have been made to a map recently.

Maximo:

Adverse Judgements: Gah! I made a map for Expanse just like this! Yours allows for a little more control with the launchpads, though.

Alaska's Got Nothing On Me: The idea is really cool, but I never have any idea which way the drones are going to go, which results in semi-cheap deaths.

Angsty: I didn't feel this met the high standards I generally have for your maps.

Arbitrary: Hooray for hallway maps!

Arkitekt: I like the drone timing here, it gives a nice strategic feel to it.

Big Monster Thing: Intense and stylish. Rock on.

Closet Monster: Unique. I have a feeling your decision to have only one vertically aiming gauss was a good one.

Common Denominator: The oneway set up was spot on here. Nice.

Daedric Temple: Interesting. I quite enjoy getting to the exit without triggering the trapdoors.

Enigmatic: We think a little too much alike, I guess. My last map submitted to Numa was named Enigmatic. Very cool map though, I like the tileset.

Grenades: A little simplistic, but it might be good as an early level.

I Quit My Day Job: A thing of beauty. Fantastic.

I'll Take My Bass Deafening: That's a very cool effect with the seeker drones. I like it.

Meely: Reminds me vaguely of your maps Plue and Spalding. Excellent flow.

Misplaced Some Files: Metanetty. The first part really reminds me of 18-2 of the main game levels.

My Mobile Army: Genuinely fun. I really like the role the laser drone played in this level.

Newsbreaks for the Poor: Style here is great. The drones are a challenge without being too overwhelming.

One Upping: A very unique map indeed. The switches that opened up the gold caches, in particular.

Partial Credit: I love the use of "5" tiles in this one. Great as far as open chaingun maps go.

Save a Lot: Wow, the enemies in this map have a real tendency to gang up on you. I still thoroughly enjoyed it, though.

Shoplifting: Brilliant. The gausses consistently kept me on my toes.

Square Holed: Quite a bit of strategy involved here. Very nice.

Strafe: As you might have guessed, I really dislike this. There's almost always going to be some luck involved if you try for the gold.

The Dividing Line: The primary motion here is creative but highly repetitive. Can't say I enjoy this too much.

The Growth Seems Exponential: Another nice one. Minor aesthetic suggestion, it might look better to change the "E" tile just to the right of the exit switch to an "8" "Q" tile to match the rest of the tileset.

Transparency: Not your best. A little bland, in my opinion.

Weak Minded: LV-esque and fantastic.


Lucidium:

Barbed Wire: The barb effect is quite cool, although aside from that the map is somewhat bland.

Beware of the Puppies: Very simple but interesting use of precision timing.

Cathedral: A nice idea. Could probably be implemented a little better, but the idea itself is solid.

Central Dense Overcast: Nothing really exciting here.

Fillin' In Time: Ah, now here's a good one. The enemy combination makes it pretty intense. I'd suggest moving the exit up a snap and a half or so, though.

Peekaboo: Holy crap! Yet another concept that I've already made into an Expanse map! Very nice job.

Sidle: What the heck? Am I missing something, or is this not beatable?

The Big Jump: Simplistic, but enjoyable.

The Displaced: Unbelievably awesome idea, but not right for Legacy. Submit this to Numa, por favor.

Why won't you leave me alone?: Kinda weird, kinda cool. Don't know about this one, really.

A Mean-spirited or spiteful remark: Nice nice. Would be fantastic as a very early level.

Angel Island: I dig the mini puzzle style, but the exit looks really odd since its hidden by the tile. And like you suggested, you might wanna do something to make sure you cant cheat.

Broken Bridge: Very cool. Theres a real sense of suspension here.

Held up by magic: Yay for delicious easy-puzzle goodness.

One of the boys: Not particularly interesting, but it gets the job done.

That was a stupid place to put them: Whoa. Surprisingly easy. Still fun though.

These bubbles dont look right: Reminds me of a much, much easier version of my Brambles and Shambles. Quite enjoyable.

Troglophile: Standard puzzle fare. Try not to make too many of these, okay?

13.6 MK: Stunning tileset. I actually found this really easy and not frustrating at all.

Confinement: A very odd array of bounce blocks and switches. I liked it for the most part though.

Equidistant: The bounce block mechanism works incredibly well, but all the gold pieces should be moved down a quarter snap so each top one doesnt overlap.

Mishmash: Decent. Cant think of much to say.


Kablizzy:

001: Interesting, but I tend to rely a lot more on the launchpads than on the oneways.

003: Nice little claustrophobic map.

004: So-so. I dont really like the way the blocky gold pattern.

005: Uh and how exactly do you get to the exit here?

007: Simple, fun map, but are all those drones really necessary?

009: Really enjoyable actually. Just old school gauss dodging with no fancy tricks.

010: Pretty good. Not too exciting.

011: Ah. Very maximoesque with the overwhelmingness of the drones.

013: Not my kind of map.

015: The oneway/bounce block combo produces a great effect, but the problem is that its way to hard to get around on them. Id suggest taking out some of the mines on some of them and adding some gold to the map.

016: Nice. Good as an early level.

017: Kinda unpolished, I think. Could be better.

018: Fantastic. I had a blast with this, well done.

019: Well-balanced and slightly above average.

021: I really like the idea behind the dual routes.

024: I likes it. The launchpad/floorguard setup is nice.

026: Nice thwump. Gah.

027: Quite nice and simple. Unpredictablish drones, slightly varying routes. Yawn.

029: Everything works as it should, enemies are effective and all that.

031: I have a big problem with placing a bunch of chainguns and gold in an open space and calling it a day. Theres no fun or reliable way to take the gold.

033: I quite like this. The tunnels are very functional as escape routes from the chainguns.

034: Kinda cool. Could see it as a Metanet level, for sure.

035: The oneway/bounce block thing works better here than in that other map.

036: Thwumps galore. Nice map.

037: Wooo! Sweet, one of the best so far. Especially the left side was great.

042: Not that great.

048: Stylish and effective.

049: That thar gold be mighty hard to get.

050: Nice tileset.

051: Nice idea. Some more gold would be nice, though, so its worth it to get it.

#165560 3 2006-04-16T23:43:24Z tktktk
Okay, I made some changes based on your comments. I also added one new level, Garden Heart, which has the same thorny vine type thing as Hanging Garden but plays much differently. See the updated pack at the bottom of this post.

Earl of Tastyburger: Changed the center gold placement and the launchpads. Now you won't be smashed back down if you jump by the exit, the exit switch, or either end.

Pinned Down: Changed name to Scramble, as that's basically the feel you get when playing this one. Removed aesthetic enemies. Moved the entire level over to the right a bit. Put two blank boxes "shooting out" at the end of most of the lasers. Lined up the gold placement with the lasers' lines of sight.

Spherical Playground: Changed the gold placement to wrap around the edges of the circles. Added some additional gold.

Flagship Dynasty: I originally had more gold at the top, but it ended up looking kinda cluttered. Also, I wanted to keep the amount of gold proportional to the risk of getting it. The bottom gold is a lot riskier to get in my opinion.

Blind Spot: That's an interesting idea, but the disorientation of looking from the ninja to the drone is supposed to be part of the challenge. I suggest focusing on the ninja while keeping the drone in your peripheral vision. Then when you see the drone get closer to the horizontal shaft, you can shift your focus to it so you can time your movements accordingly.

Hanging Garden: Got rid of the four launchpads on the right and the rightmost trapdoor. Added a trapdoor on the left and moved one of them a bit to the right, plus a floorguard and a "3" tile on the ground. Should be somewhat easier now.

Garden Heart: Changed the petals on the chaingun flower. Makes getting to that upper switch quite a bit easier.

Quote: Guest, April 13, 2006 08:48 pm
"Clovic: Just think about this for a second. Doesn't it make sense to give the highest ratings to maps you enjoy the most? The primary factor in deciding how you rate a map should always be how much fun you have playing it."

No I disagree.  While enjoyment is a major factor in how good a map is, it is not the only major factor, nor is it always the most important.  There is also the flow of the level to consider, the enemy and gold placement, the aesthetic value of the map, any new or innovative ideas, how fun/not fun the tile set is.  There have been maps that I've down-right thought were just bloody annoying and not fun at all that I have given 4.5's to and there are also maps that I've absolutely loved that I've given 2.5's and 3's to.  How much fun with a map you have is important, but it's not even close to the only, or most important, thing you should consider in my opinion. 

But I suppose that brings up another point, everyone has different priority's when rating maps.  People look for different things, find different things fun/boring, find different things ugly.  To you fun-factor is the most important, to me it is on an equal plane with about 5 other things.
Just think about this. Do you play video games to admire the pretty item placement, or do you play them to have fun? Some of the things you mentioned, such as flow, factor into the fun of the map. In fact, you actually used the phrase "fun/not fun" to describe one of your categories, which shows that you actually agree with me more than you think. But if for example you play a map that has innovative ideas but plays like crap, can you look me in the eye and say that you'll give it a good rating?

#169441 11 2006-04-29T05:56:28Z tktktk
All right, guys. It's taken me a while, but I've managed to scrounge up the basic framework for this thing. If there's anything major that I've missed, that needs to be expanded upon, or that you don't agree with, please let me know. Feedback on the part that's being posted on May 1st would be particularly helpful; it's looking a little on the short side at the moment.

The following will be posted (hopefully) on May 1st:
Quote
Welcome, friends, to the Hall of Fame! The HoF is a Legacy production, an annual awards show meant to be a supplement to the Dronies, so that one show is concluded every six months. It's not just a display of the best maps of the year, but a showcase of the greatest maps of all time. It will include all playable maps, including Metanet levels and others that haven't been submitted to Numa. Regardless of whether they're action, puzzle, survival, or race maps, those honored in the Hall of Fame will be only the very best, the ones that are truly deserving of legendary status.

Here are the rules for nominations:
1) Any playable map from any place or date will be eligible for nomination, even the in-game levels. That means they don't necessarily need to have been submitted to Numa, but maps such as DDAs cannot be nominated.
2) You may nominate as many maps as you wish, within reason.
3) You should nominate maps that you consider to be the best and that you believe have stood (or will stand) the test of time and become true classics.
4) You must PM your nominations to me or one of the other Legacy members.
5) Nominations must be submitted no later than midnight on May 31st.
6) The Legacy team reserves the right to decline your nominations, and in this unlikely event we will inform you of why they were declined.

All right, kids, off we go. Get nominating!

The following will be posted on June 1st:
Quote
Well, friends, the nominations have been submitted, and now it's time to vote. Here are the nominees:

[Insert nominees here]

Here are the rules for voting:
1) You may not vote for your own maps.
2) You may vote for up to five of the nominated maps, ranking them from 1st choice to 5th. If you want to vote for less you may, but we strongly encourage you to vote for five.
3) The Legacy team reserves the right to decline your votes, and in this highly unlikely event we will inform you of why they were declined. We will only do it with very good reason. We may also tell people about it in this thread to get a second opinion.
4) You must PM your votes to me or one of the other Legacy members.
5) Your votes must be submitted no later than midnight on June 31st. The final results will be posted shortly afterwards.
6) Preferably, don't tell other people who you voted for.

Scoring System:
Each person can nominate up to five maps, ranking them from 1st to 5th. Each rank will receive a point value as follows:

1st choice: 5 points
2nd choice: 4 points
3rd choice: 3 points
4th choice: 2 points
5th choice: 1 point

Now as this is an awards show with multiple winners, the voting results will be accessible to the public in as unbiased a manner as possible. That means we'll show the number of votes each maps got and all that, but without glorifying the maps that got the most votes over the others.

A small number of truly legendary base maps will be selected by the Legacy team, and will be put into the Hall of Fame regardless of the number of votes they receive. The base maps will be kept a secret until the public-chosen additions are revealed. The nominations list that the public will be voting on come June 1st will include nominations from other people along with the base maps.

Here are the maps I'm nominating as base maps. I tried to base my picks not on the ones I personally like the most, but rather the ones I think all knowledgeable players would agree are "classics":

Artificial Intelligence by LittleViking001
Coalition by LittleViking001
Contraction by nevermore
Convention by LittleViking001
Deceptive by Lucidium
Flight by maximo
Flipside by maximo
Framework by tktktk
Jacks by Lucidium
Marathon by maximo
Mother Thumping Impossible by blue_tetris
Mount Doom by maximo
Plue by maximo
Pressed for Time by Lucidium
0-0 The Motherlode by Metanet Software
The Crazy Miner by formica

Please comment on which ones of these base maps you agree and disagree on, and nominate your own as well. Remember, you're voting for only the most "legendary" maps that are widely recognized as all-time greats. It's probably a good idea just to have older maps in here, because they've had time to accumulate prestige and all that.

Aside from games, I think price point is going to have the most influence on how the console war plays out.

One thing that jumped out at me in this thread was that the PS3 has Blu-ray technology that would cost $1000 on its own. Assuming it's true, that is a good deal for the consumer, but it makes one wonder. How much money is Sony going to be losing on each system sold, even when they're sold at the ludicrous price of $600?

And just to clear up any misconceptions about the Wii's price, the only thing Nintendo has said specifically is that it will be under $250. My personal belief is that it will be somewhere in the range of $199.99-$249.99. Also, as far as games go, paying 10 dollars more PS3 games than Wii games seems pretty ridiculous to me. Particularly because of my personal belief that Wii games (particularly first party ones) will generally be superior.

#9259 1 2006-06-05T02:47:58Z tktktk
Well, friends, the nominations have been submitted. Fifty maps have been selected, the cream of the crop. Now it's time to see what maps all of you think are the true legends. Here are the rules for voting:

The Voting Rules:
1) You must PM your votes to either tktktk or sweep.
2) You may vote for up to five of the nominated maps, ranking them from 1st choice to 5th (see the scoring system below). If you want to vote for less you may, but we strongly encourage you to vote for five.
3) Your votes must be submitted no later than midnight on June 30th. The final results will be posted shortly afterwards.
4) You may not vote for your own maps.
5) Preferably, don't tell other people who you voted for.
6) The Legacy team reserves the right to decline your votes, and in this highly unlikely event we will inform you of why they were declined. We will only do it with very good reason. We may also tell people about it in this thread to get a second opinion.

The Scoring System:
Each person can nominate up to five maps, ranking them from 1st to 5th (1st being highest). Each rank will receive a point value as follows:

1st choice: 5 points
2nd choice: 4 points
3rd choice: 3 points
4th choice: 2 points
5th choice: 1 point

The number of points that each map receives will be totaled, and the 20 maps that receive the most points out of the 50 will be inducted into the Hall of Fame. The ten base maps referred to in the nominations thread were inducted automatically, and are not included in the voting list.

And now, without further ado, the nominees:

#9704 1 2006-06-26T08:30:33Z tktktk
Read something in a book several years ago (a biography of mathematician Paul Erdos) that I found pretty interesting. Did you know that some infinities are larger than others? Here, I'll show you. My apologies if this explanation is a bit confusing, but here goes:

We define Set #1 as being the same size as Set #2 if every member of Set #1 corresponds to a member of Set #2. However, if there are members of Set #1 that don't have a corresponding member in Set #2, Set #1 is larger than Set #2.

For example, the set of all even numbers is the same size as the set of all integers (or whole numbers):

1-----2
2-----4
3-----6
4-----8
5-----10
Ad infinitum

And so is the set of all squares, all primes, and even all fractions. But is the set of all decimals the same size as the set of all integers? Say we could write out every single decimal number onto some very large sheet of paper (keep in mind that this is an infinite list of these numbers stretch on infinitely):

1-----.138109523652309486...
2-----.987234561439874569...
3-----.239847562348527952...
4-----.792345216084237695...
5-----.269875126125526341...
Ad infinitum

Now, what if we took the 1st decimal place in the first number, the 2nd decimal place in the second number, the 3rd decimal place in the third, ad infinitum, and made a number from that?:

.138109523652309486...
.987234561439874569...
.236847562348527952...
.792345216084237695...
.269875126125526341...
Ad infinitum

Makes:

.18637...

That's all well and good, but that number is also on our list. But what if we added 1 to each decimal place of the number?:

.18637...
+
.11111...
=
.29748..., our new number.

Now, this is the hardest part to wrap your head around, but stay with me. That number we just made is nowhere on our list. How do we know that? Well, we just go back and compare our new number to each number on our original list. Notice anything?

Look closer. Remember that the "2" in .29748... came from the first digit in our first number, which happened to be a "1", with 1 added onto it. See the problem there? There is no possible way that our new number could be the same as our first number, because that first digit is different.

In the same way, the "9" in our .29748... was taken from the second digit of the second number, which was an "8". They can't be the same number, either, because the second different is different. The same goes for the third digit of the third number, and for all of the rest of the numbers on our list. So, what does that mean?

Firstly, it means that our new number, .29748..., most definitely isn't on our list. But wait, wasn't our list supposed to have all of the possible decimal numbers on it? It was, but we seemed to have missed one. (And, by the way, we could go through that same little experiment again, and get an infinite number of numbers that weren't on the list.) That means there's a member of the Decimal Set that doesn't correspond to the Integer Set. Soo, that means...

The set of all decimals is larger than the set of all integers. We've come upon a larger infinity. The regular ol' integer infinity is also known by mathematicians as aleph-zero, and our newfangled decimal infinity is aleph-one.

And now we all have headaches. Happy fun time?
#194681 4 2006-06-26T08:39:11Z tktktk
KA: A book called The Man Who Loved Only Numbers, a biography of mathematician Paul Erdos. I read it for fun, because I'm weird like that.

Pembie: Basically, there are more decimal numbers than there are whole numbers. And since there's an infinite amount of whole numbers, there has to be a bigger infinity for decimal numbers.
#194914 70 2006-06-26T18:56:18Z tktktk
Wedgie: Your concept of infinity is rather faulty. Infinity is literally the place where parallel lines intersect. I know that doesn't make sense, but neither does infinity. In the same way, it's the point where a series such as: .9, .99, .999, .9999... gets to just plain ol' one.

You guys don't seem to understand that this isn't even a subject of debate in the mathematical community.

.999 (recurring) has been PROVEN in dozens of different ways to equal 1.

All mathematicians, as far as I know, accept this as fact. I'm really tempted to lock this thread right now to avoid further ridiculousness.

#195872 136 2006-06-28T17:16:05Z tktktk
Quote: obby, June 28, 2006 04:16 pm
And I would be GLAD to show you where he said that. You even quoted it from my link! LOOK UP!

Here is a quote from my page.

Quote: Dr. Math
.9 is not 1; neither is .999, nor .9999999999. In fact if you stop the
expansion of 9s at any finite point, the fraction you have (like .9999
= 9999/10000) is never equal to 1.
Holy. Living. Crap.
Frigging look at the quote, and you'll see why I linked to it. It says that AT ANY FINITE POINT the fraction will not equal one. Do you understand that? It only applies to the non-infinite.

However.

As the fraction approaches infinity, it equals one.

Perhaps you haven't done limits before in math class. Imagine the graph of a curved line. As the line moves from left to right, it is also moving upwards, but at a slower and slower rate, sorta like a 4S curve in N. As the line gets further and further to the right, that line gets closer and closer to the line y=1. Now, with a problem like this, we would say that the limit as x approaches infinity is one. This isn't something I made up. This is something we do all the time in our math class.

And here are quotes from both our links that state that .999... equals 1:

Quote: Your link
Thus, if you are going to assign a value to .9999... (going on
forever), the only sensible value is 1.
Quote: Your link
You can show for all such examples that doing the arithmetic
on the series produces "reasonable" results:

Since:

1/3 = .333333...
2/3 = .666666...

1/3 + 2/3 = .999999... = 1.
Quote: My link which is just as valid because your link uses it as a reference and it comes from the same site
In modern mathematics, the string of symbols 0.9999... = 1 is understood to mean "the infinite sum 9/10 + 9/100 + 9/1000 + ...". This in turn is shorthand for "the limit of the sequence of numbers

9/10,
9/10 + 9/100,
9/10 + 9/100 + 9/1000,
...."


One can show that this limit is 9/10 + 9/100 + 9/1000 ... using Analysis, and a proof really isn't all that hard (we all believe it intuitively anyway); a reference can be found in any of the Analysis texts referenced at the end of this message. Then all we have left to do is show that this sum really does equal 1:

Proof: 0.9999... = Sum 9/10^n
(n=1 -> Infinity)

= lim sum 9/10^n
(m -> Infinity) (n=1 -> m)

= lim .9(1-10^-(m+1))/(1-1/10)
(m -> Infinity)

= lim .9(1-10^-(m+1))/(9/10)
(m -> Infinity)

= .9/(9/10)

= 1

Edit: And listen to maximo, he knows what he's talking about.

#200230 21 2006-07-08T07:23:19Z tktktk
Here's Raigan's post, paraphrased and summarized:

Quote: Raigan, 2006-07-08T00:56:16Z
The Next Game
We refuse to rush TNG because we intend to add to this game for a while after it's come out, and we don't want to have the same problems of not being able to implement new features. Things are coming along very nicely. Most of the design has been completed and is working well, and almost all of the tech is finished, and we're really excited by how it's shaping up.

TNG will almost certainly not be released by the end of the summer. The game will be done as soon as possible, but we won't be releasing this game until we feel as good about it as we did with N.

N v1.5
We've also been working a bit on the next update to N. This is something that we'd like some feedback on:

We also want to integrate user levels more fully into the game. The idea is that it will be easy for people to drop in different sets of levels/episodes which will be identical to the current built-in levels in terms of functionality. Each set would be able to have a highscore server. We would continue to host the highscores for the "official" levels, and anyone who wished to could run a server for a set of episodes/levels.

Increased cheating in the highscores has led us to consider freezing the current highscores, and starting anew with a rewritten system that has more security measures built in. If we restart the highscores, we could make some adjustments to the gameplay itself. We don't want to change anything drastically, we simply want to fix some of the things we feel we could have done better, such as:
  • Glitchy stuttering when running up slopes.
  • Drones which can only move in 90 degree increments. We had originally intended the surface-following drones to move smoothly across the actual surface of the world.
  • Other surface-related things, like allowing floorchasers to move along any surface.
  • Seeker drones don't always chase you predictably, and we'd like to change this.
  • The chaingun drone is too random. It should fire an arc of bullets as it does now, but in such a way that if you're within that arc, you will die no matter what.
  • Corner jumping has made us think about implementing a slightly different collision system to make it easier to jump. For example, there would be a larger window of opportunity for timing jumps.
No matter what we do, we will preserve the current gameplay as a "classic" mode, so that all of your user-made levels/etc. aren't broken. This is all hypothetical since we first need to finish TNG, but we wanted to let you know what we've been considering. We're still going to release the source code, but we don't want to do so until we've finished N.
Things really seem to be going well, and I'm more excited than ever for the future. Although it's a shame that all that work would be wasted, I'm all for restarting the highscores if it means that all the little problems can be fixed and new features can be added.

#200409 44 2006-07-08T21:15:11Z tktktk
Here's my two cents on the potential changes made to N that people seem to be concerned about:

Quote: Raigan, 2006-07-08T00:56:16Z
Surface-following drones that move smoothly across the actual surface of the world.
To me, sweep's suggestion of simply making this another setting in Ned would be ideal.

Quote: Raigan, 2006-07-08T00:56:16Z
The chaingun drone is too random. It should fire an arc of bullets as it does now, but in such a way that if you're within that arc, you will die no matter what.
Although it will make the chaingun an even more formidable opponent, I fully support this. I've been a mapmaker long enough to know that randomness is always a bad thing.

Quote: Raigan, 2006-07-08T00:56:16Z
Corner jumping has made us think about implementing a slightly different collision system to make it easier to jump. For example, there would be a larger window of opportunity for timing jumps.
I'm sure a lot of highscorers would resent making their fancy tricks easy for new players to duplicate. I'm on the fence with this one; it really depends on how something like this is implemented.

Quote: Raigan, 2006-07-08T15:52:28Z
By "restart" the highscores, we were trying to distinguish from "reset" -- we won't delete the existing scores, they'll simply be frozen for posterity, so that you can view them but not get new ones.
Even better.

#10103 1 2006-07-16T19:22:50Z tktktk
Those of you that have been around long enough might remember this thread I posted about two years ago. My family goes to Sweden every other year or so for about a month to visit my mom's relatives, and that time has come again. This year we also happen to be making a stop in New York City. So anyway, I'll be gone from July 17th to August 23rd. While I will be bringing a laptop, I won't have access to N or the internet. So, that's the bad news.

The good news is that, first of all, I'll be sure to take advantage of any chance I get to stop by the forums. It may be several times, or it may be none at all, but it's a possibility at least. Secondly, those who enjoyed my short story Angel Wings will be glad to know that since I'll have plenty of time on my hands I'll be hard at work on expanding the story into a full-blown novel. I've got most of the plot together, and now I just have to get it all down on paper (or more accurately the computer screen). No guarantees it'll work out, of course. #11850 1 2006-08-27T06:55:19Z tktktk
Welcome to the N Wiki Level Article Project (aka the NWLA), where our mission is to create an article for each level of N in the N Wiki. First of all, let me state the overall goal of creating these level articles:

We want not only to provide information on each of the levels in the game, but to essentially recreate the N Episode Help Site and Thread (NEHS and NEHT) here in wiki format, so any player that needs help with a level can simply be referred to that level's article.

We will be splitting into two groups. One group will be doing screenshots, and the other, walkthroughs. Pick whichever one you want to be in. I will be creating the basic framework for most of the level articles. But if you're doing an article that hasn't been created yet, just type in {{subst:Level}}, and then once it's been created you can add the screenshot or walkthrough you wanted to post.

Walkthrough Group
pokemaniac1342
RincewindSW

Guidelines for Walkthrough Group
  • Please use walkthroughs from the NEHS, NEHT, or AEW whenever possible, simply because it makes your job easier and get things done quicker.
  • Please use a semiformal style when writing your walkthroughs.
  • Specify the subject matter of each walkthrough (i.e., completion, gold, speed, highscore).
  • Try not to be overly biased or refer to yourself within the walkthrough.
  • When copying from the NEHS, NEHT, or AEW, please site your source (look here for an example).
  • Feel free to edit any walkthroughs you've copied from the NEHS, NEHT, or AEW whenever necessary to comply with these guidelines and maintain the consistency of the other level articles.
  • If you'd like to add a screenshot with arrows and other indicators added as a visual aid for your walkthough, feel free to do so, but don't put it where primary screenshots normally go. The reasons for this are that (1) walkthroughs are not the only purpose of the level articles and (2) there may be more than one walkthrough for one level article, which would make things considerably more complicated.
Screenshot Group
...

Guidelines for Screenshot Group
  • Follow these instructions, courtesy of Scott5114:
    Take a screenshot, crop it, and save to your disk, preferably as a PNG. Don't resize it. Go to the page Special:Upload. Tell it where to find the file on your hard disk, come up with a name for it on-wiki (usually the number of the level is good - e.g. "88-4.png"), and add a description. Once the file is transferred you can get it to appear in an article by passing the name of it as the "image" parameter for the Infobox Level template. It will be resized automatically to fit, and a user can click the image to view the original version. If you put [[Category:Level screenshots]] in the description field, it'll appear in that category, which I can see functioning as a level gallery of sorts.
  • Please post primary screenshots in the indicated section of each article. It should read: |image = [Insert name of uploaded image here]
  • If you'd like to add a screenshot with arrows and other indicators added as a visual aid for a walkthough, feel free to do so, but please display them elsewhere on the same page as the primary screenshot. The reasons for this are that (1) walkthroughs are not the only purpose of the level articles and (2) there may be more than one walkthrough for one level article, which would make things considerably more confusing. Use the following format:

    [[Image:Walkthroughaid.png|thumb|270px|Right|Description]]

    Add the name of the screenshot where it says "Walkthroughaid", and a short description identifying the pic where it says "Description".
The Task List

This is where you'll find info on what we'll be doing in the NWLA, in order of priority. The ones on top are most important.

1. Create the most-needed level articles (list coming soon).
2. Create articles using walkthroughs from NEHS, NEHT, and AEW.
3. Create articles for the 0th column levels.
4. Create articles for levels in other columns.

#221539 51 2006-08-30T06:30:02Z tktktk
A few tidbits from the forum FAQ that I enjoyed:

Quote
Q: What is the motive behind this conspiracy?
A: The motive is unknown.

Q: If you don't even have a possible motive, why do you say there is a conspiracy?
A: Well it's quite simple really; if the earth is in fact flat, then the the governments must be lying when they say it isn't.

Q: How are the world governments organised enough to carry out this conspiracy?
A: They only appear to be disorganised to make the conspiracy seem implausible.
Hear that folks? Everything's organized and under control. You know all that conflict in the Middle East? Just another part of a conspiracy to make us all believe the world is round. Makes sense to me.

Quote
Q: What's underneath the Earth?
A: This is unknown. Some believe it to be just rocks, others believe the Earth rests on the back of four elephants and a turtle.
This is probably a joke, but with all the other bizarre elements of their theory, you never know...

Quote
Q: Why does gravity vary with altitiude?
A: The moon and stars have a slight gravitational pull.

Q: How is it that the Earth does not have a gravitiational pull, but stars and the moon do?
A: This argument is a non sequitur. You might as well ask, "How is it that snakes do not have legs, but dogs and cats do?" Snakes are not dogs or cats. The Earth is not a star or the moon. It doesn't follow that each must have exactly the properties of the others, and no more.
Oh, I get it. So the sun and moon have some magical property that gives them gravity. It has nothing to do with mass, it's just some arbitrary concept that we can mold and shape to keep our theory intact. Let's just start doling out gravity to whichever heavenly bodies we feel like, and withhold it from the others. Sound good?

#226157 42 2006-09-09T06:04:07Z tktktk
While I remember, I just wanna post about one of my biggest grammar pet peeves. When you're referring to a company or organization, you treat it as a singular, not a plural. In other words, instead of thinking of it as a group of individuals, think of it as a single entity. For example:

Wrong: Nintendo are releasing a game soon.
Right: Nintendo is releasing a game soon.

Wrong: They are a big company.
Right: It is a big company.

You wouldn't think it would be such a problem, but I see people make this mistake all the time, even in mailbag responses for videogame sites, when they should be used to referring to companies.

#232299 44 2006-09-23T06:42:26Z tktktk
In terms of pure fun, I just want to highlight one of the few games that has torn me away from N long enough for me to beat it: Donkey Kong Jungle Beat for Gamecube. It's a platformer controlled by bongo drums. Yes, you read that right.

And yet as unlikely as it may seem, the game is basically a gigantic wad o' fun. The controls and the combo system take a few minutes to get the hang of but after that they're completely intuitive, and you'll be stringing combos across nearly entire levels in no time just by clapping and banging drums like a madman. If it sounds dumb, it's because words don't really do it justice. It really needs to be experienced to understand. Now, the game isn't perfect, and it's probably not even among my all-time favorites. It's not your typical platformer, nor is it an epic quest with tons of replay value. It's just simple fun, and that's all there is to it.

Plus, all that drumming adds up to a pretty decent workout. No joke.

All right, new information on priorities. This is pretty much how things will be operating from here on out:

The Task List

This is where you'll find info on what we'll be doing in the NWLA, in order of priority. The ones on top are most important.

1. Create the most-needed level articles (list coming soon).
2. Create articles using walkthroughs from NEHS, NEHT, and AEW.
3. Create articles for the 0th column levels.
4. Create articles for levels in other columns.
By the way, please check the first post for this sort of thing at regular intervals. That's where I'll be doing most of my updates, including the task list.

We'll be doing number 1 on that list pretty much exclusively until it's finished. After that we'll move on to articles that are easiest to create, namely the ones that already have walkthroughs written for them. The only hard part there will be actually finding the walkthroughs to copy over, but it shouldn't be too much of a problem. After that, we'll do Episodes 00 through 09, more or less in order, because that's almost certainly the most played column, particularly by new players. While we're doing those things you guys can be working on some random level articles on the side if you want, but our focus is going to be based on this strategy.

So, within the next day or two we'll have a list of the levels that we most need articles for, based on how many people have asked for help with them on the forums. We'll go in order with those, assigning certain people to individual level articles. For example, I might ask Rincewind to write a walkthrough (or copy one from NEHS or elsewhere) for 5-0, and 29403 to add a screenshot. You can request certain levels from that list, or decline to do one you're assigned to, but that's generally how it will work.

Also, I didn't mention it before, but if people who are signing up could state a preference of doing walkthroughs vs. screenshots, that would be great. You folks who are already a part of the project, I'm just gonna assume you're with the same group unless you say otherwise.

By the way, I encourage you guys to spread the word around about the project, put a link in your sig, anything that'll get noticed. I'm really excited about the future of this project, and the more people it has working on it, the more likely it will be to flourish.

#294327 44 2007-02-06T06:51:33Z tktktk
It's amazing to see how many mistakes Sony has made with the PS3, and how much bad press there is out there as a result. This timeline that I found a few weeks ago chronicles a lot of the blunders surrounding the console (it's the first two posts in the thread). Basically, this is my thought process when I look at the PS3:

The high price of the PS3 means a lower install base.
Lower install base means lower game sales.
High development costs combined with low game sales means low profit for developers.
Low profit means the PS3 won't see many exclusive titles.

At that point it becomes a vicious cycle. Fewer exclusives plus a continued high price (Sony can't drop the price very easily due to the $200-$300 hit it's taking on each console sold) means continued low install base, meaning continued low game sales, and so on and so forth. In order to break this cycle, Sony is going to have to part with a lot of money to either secure exclusives or lower the price. Either way, the company certainly has its work cut out for it.

Okay, I don't know if you've looked in the other threads, but generally what we do is have everyone play everyone else's maps and write just a line or two commenting about each, what we like and dislike and so forth. Boole and You - The drone paths make for some interesting gameplay. I completely ignored the launchpads during my first runthrough, but they definitely add to the flow of getting the gold if used correctly.

Carbon Marriage - Awesome tileset, and a very unique map. I wasn't sure how to get the exit switch at first; I like the puzzle element that gives it. The rocket placement was great as well; it made things kind of awkward, but in a challenging rather than a cumbersome way.

In Absentia - I liked the way the drones were set up. Getting back up after taking the exit switch was interesting as well.

Sloapes - Best of the five. The simplicity of the gameplay is great. Getting both bunches of gold as well as maneuvering around the final couple of floorguards at the end was a lot of fun.

The Big Eat - Very nice. The tileset is simultaneously terrifying and adorable, and the final jump to get to the exit is quite exhilarating.

#362729 209 2007-09-06T18:47:52Z tktktk
Here's my advice to people who are feeling overwhelmed by the prospect of making so many maps in such a short time.

You don't need an amazing new concept for each map. If you're not sure where to start, just very quickly put something down without second guessing yourself, whether it's a blob of E tiles, a cloud of bounce blocks, or whatever. Then fill in whatever enemies and other items fit best with what you already have. It's easier said than done, sure, but the point is that if you overthink things you're going to end up taking a lot longer for what might be only a slightly more polished map. Plus, this way you get to break out of your style a bit and experiment with things you haven't tried before.


Edit: Also, five of my Vehemence 2 maps are now up on Numa, in case anyone's interested.

#363331 213 2007-09-08T19:56:47Z tktktk
I'm just trying to think of some more advice for you guys, because I understand how overwhelming the idea of making so many maps in such a short time looks.

Another way to shorten the normally massive amount of time it takes to make 100 maps is to just make some of them smaller. If you notice, not very many of my maps used the entire space available for gameplay. For example, just put three E blocks down hovering in the middle of the maps, and build a bit of gameplay around them, or start with the map filled with tiles and just excavate a few corridors.

One more thing... if you get even the tiniest hint of an idea, use it, no matter how trivial it seems. Even something simple like "put clumps of three oneways throughout the map" or "have a floorguard on every flat surface" can easily turn into a full fledged map with a small amount of effort. I started out a lot of my maps wondering how I was going to make it work, and ended with something I was actually quite satisfied with.

#364136 65 2007-09-11T08:36:07Z tktktk
Smartalco, it's the pre-alpha version, so no complaining.

Also, there's an interview with Mare and Raigan here. The more interesting bits:

Quote: Joystiq Interview
Any details about release estimates or platform for Robotology (Metanet's second game)?

Ah, Robotology. It's taking forever, and has been delayed by N+, which has required more time and work than we thought. But we should be able to get back to it shortly, and are planning to enter it in next year's IGF.

It'll be released on Mac/PC first, but we're not sure where it'll go from there.


Are you done done done with N after this, or do you foresee a return to the project after Robotology?

Well, we're planning on releasing an official web-playable version of N in the near future, and there's still an update to N for PC that needs to be done... and when we're done those, it'll probably be just about time to get started on N, or NN, or whatever the sequel will be called... so yes, probably, but first we have a few other game ideas we need to get finished!


Since you challenged me to N+ (and I chickened out), what kinds of multiplayer options will be available in the Xbox version? And do you feel that this changes the experience of the game beyond, you know, having another person there?

There are three flavours of multiplayer: one cooperative and two competitive (survival and race). Multiplayer mode isn't *too* different from sinleplayer mode, gameplay-wise, but it certainly has some interesting new gameplay mechanics. For example, cooperative mode: in some levels your "roles" are not identical. You can either distract the enemies while your friend unlocks the exit, or you can make the treacherous journey to the exit yourself, while your friend holds off the robot hordes. You have to have flexible skills, and be ready to change direction immediately if necessary.


Are your games aimed at hardcore N lovers or new players? Or was N+ designed with both in mind?

N+ was definitely designed with both in mind. First we leveled out the learning curve and added a bunch of very easy/tutorial levels so new players wouldn't feel so intimidated. For the hardcore N fans we made some creative levels that can be traversed using either beginner or advanced methods, so they won't be completely bored by the easier levels. We also added a "hardcore" unlockable for those that want more, and more difficult levels, once they've beaten the game.

Great stuff over all. Keep in mind when looking at these that it's my first playthrough for most of them, and I'll probably become more opinionated one way or the other as time after I go through them again. But anyway, here are my comments for the first half:


Aclausted: Nice, a good start. Symmetry and thwumps both work well.

Acousted: Great. I especially like the corner gold setup.

Anthill: Cool, but those zap drones are really merciless.

Beacon of Distress: Interesting concept.

Bigheaded: Brilliant. Everythings perfect.

Blackout: The setup is unusual, but I love it.

Boxet: Whoa. It works, but its not one of my favorites.

Bumbed to Business Class: Man, you really have a way of setting up drone paths that psyche me out.

Bungie Gulch: Tough map, but very cool. The mindfield in the middle is a bit frustrating.

Call it a Day: A bit on the long side, but I like the ideas that come into play here.

Common Denominator/Remake: Very flowy and a lot of fun to play. I like Remake better except for the thwumps, which dont really seem to add a lot to the map.

Confussion: I like this, except for the fact that the oneways on the right side are cheatable. I thought it would be tough to do, but I actually got it on my first try. I would suggest actually getting rid of the down-facing oneways and making that a legitimate route, though, because it was a lot of fun (although you might want to make it a bit harder, so the two options stay balanced).

Contrary To: way to easy ibeat it frst try 0/5. Seriously, though, another very nice one.

Cooperation Cooperation: This one has a classic feel to it that I really like.

Crey: Its different and cool.

Daedric Temple: The tileset and launchpads gives it a lot of potential for high-flyingness.

Debt: In the lower half of your maps, I think, but its nice for a change of pace.

Decoded: I like the idea, but rocket + mines + thwumps + drones = too intense.

Dont Wake Daddy: I had a map kinda like this in Expanse, but this ones so much cooler.

Down Scale: Cool ideas, but they dont really play like theyre supposed to be part of the same map.

Dronn: Like Metanet on steroids.

Easy Come: Love it.

Evil in Me: Too convoluted for my tastes, both in style and to a lesser extent in gameplay.

Family Reunion: I like the right and middle parts of this more than the left.

Fuzzy Dice: Freakin cool. The enemies are all great.

Glar: I like the idea, but its a little on the long side. Maybe get rid of the third column and have it end at the bottom. And also, the gold looks a little off.

Globed: Not bad. It really helps that the partitions are made out of bounce blocks and not tiles.

Grenades: Simple gameplay, great tileset. I like it.

I dont know: The drones make things crazy, but not frustrating, so its fine.

I pictured it differently: Not great, not terrible.

Im Not Going In: Reminds me a bit of 79-4 beach head in the main game.

Its like something out of Shakespeare: I cant really find the flow of this one. There might be something specific youre supposed to do to get around, but I dont know what it is.

Lady in the Chaingun: I like it, but it does suffer from a bit of Chaingun Randomness Syndrome.

Lag: Man I suck at avoiding seeker drones. I liked the idea, but I found it frustrating, probably due to my own incompetence.

Lost in Dyslexia: Its okay. The first switch is really weird to get, but it was probably meant to be.

Make a Wish: Well, this is definitely different from your usual style. I like it.

Make Up Your Mind: Nice mini-challengy goodness. The only thing is that figuring out which switches not to get is basically trial and error.

Marginally Irrational: A lot of the gold has no threat attached to it, but then I guess thats a result of the style, so I cant complain.

Misconcept: Oh, man, I love this tileset. The guy looks so genuinely confused.

Mistakes Happen: I really enjoyed the parts with the oneway blocks, gauss and floorguard, and the rest was just okay.

Mixed Emotions: Its different and I love it.

My Bag of Tricks Runs Deep: The switches-among-gold idea is great.

Nope, I Refuse: Very cool, I like.

Notch: Flows well.

Ode to Satisfaction: Solid, interesting map.

Ode to Signature: Neat little drone path thing, but it feels kinda rough, more like a test level than a full-fledged map.

Painful: Nice use of rotational symmetry, and the gausses work well too.

Partial Credit: All good, except for the second highest gold cache, which I cant figure out how to get without being subjected to random chaingun deaths.

Passion: Excellent. One thing, though, is that when faced with that seeker drone my first instinct was to lure it through the normal door, and that kind of negated the challenge of the right side somewhat.

Pentacost: I love the design, but for some reason I found it really difficult to get to the top part of the map.

#365129 6 2007-09-15T07:18:23Z tktktk
Hostages: Both the style and the gameplay are cool. The optional switches make things interesting, although they might have been a little "too" optional - meaning, getting past the seeker drones was pretty easy even without them.

I Built This House: I love the diversity of the different routes you can take. But again, though, I think the switches are "too" optional, it was quite easy to just get into the exit switch area and get back out again. As a side note, I don't know if this was intentional or not (and it's fine if it was), but the right bounce block is a quarter snap higher than the left one. Just thought I'd mention it in case you were going for symmetry there.

Minutes For Memories: Great stuff. The gauss makes things a little frustrating, but you've got the tiles in there to block its line of sight, so it balances out the difficulty a bit.

Parts: What a cool style. The rocket setup did make things frustrating at times though.

Red Room: Wow. You managed to take the sort of map that would ordinarily feel very generic and make it fresh. The gold placement in the gauss room really spiced up the look of the map.

This Tower was built with Babel: Getting in and out of the exit switch area was kind of frustrating at times. I know moving the normal doors too far would ruin the challenge, but maybe one or two tiles down would do the trick.

Today has Wings: I didn't like the rocket part until I figured out that there's actually a specific way of doing it that's actually quite fun. The different parts of the map fit together a bit strangely, but they're pretty enjoyable overall.

While You Wait: Simply awesome. Love it. The only issue here is the zap drone. It looks like you've allowed an opportunity to get around it while it's still in the tube, but I can't do the map fast enough to get there in time.

In my tests, I've found that the best place for the zap drone at the start is in the same horizontal row, but directly above the leftmost gauss. It would probably work one tile to the right of that as well, but it would be cutting it pretty close. Unfortunately this isn't optimal for the all gold route, but it's the only way I can think of to make it so you can get past the drone before it goes up the chute. If you want to make sure the gold route doesn't come to a bottleneck where you're waiting around for five seconds for the drone to come out, the only thing I can think of is to put some more gold in somewhere so it'll take longer to get everything.

Overall, it looks very good, but there are a couple of general problems I want to address.

First, the difficulty is generally pretty high on these, so a lot of the time I got the impression that I was playing through one of your Super Hard Columns, and that's not the vibe I should be getting from something in a Legacy pack. So, try to vary your maps a bit more in difficulty, and make a few easier ones to balance out the ones you have now.

Second, you have a lot of fantastic ideas, but a lot of them are used in ways that feel kind of unrefined or test level-ish. A lot of what you have now is a great fit for Ampersand, but not for the main Zenith pack. Some of the concepts can be reworked into something more suitable. In the future, don't be afraid to try out new ideas, but focus a lot of your efforts on integrating them into a normal action level format.

Again, what you have is great, it's just that in its current form, some of it doesn't fit with the style of maps that we're aiming for with Legacy.

#17682 1 2007-10-26T22:32:25Z tktktk


Why wasn't there a thread for this already? This is Super Mario Galaxy, guys. Super. Mario. Galaxy. It's set to be one of the best games of this generation of consoles. Virtually all impressions reviews have been insanely positive. And the game comes out just a few weeks from now is out right now. If you're not excited for this game, either you will be after this thread, or there may be something wrong with you. Prepare yourself.

Also, if you have any questions about the game, feel free to ask.

Warning: Thread may contain spoilers: screenshots, impressions, linked videos, etc.[/b]

The Basics
Quote: Wikipedia; with some edits
Most of the game is set in outer space along a vast chain of miniature planetoids and other space matter, though many levels consist of huge areas to explore.

Mario is capable of jumping or launching from planet to planet in order to gather items and defeat enemies. Gravity plays a significant role in the game, as each planet has a gravitational force that prevents Mario from drifting off into space, which allows the player to effortlessly circumnavigate rounded objects. The varying degrees of gravity also have an effect on Mario's ability to jump, and can be used to pull Mario toward certain planetoids while in mid-flight. Like previous 3D Mario games, the main objective is to collect Power Stars, which are awarded by completing tasks or defeating enemies. The game's central hub is set in the Comet Observatory, which is divided into six themed areas. Distributed among these six worlds are 40 "galaxies", or levels with 1 to 6 stars each. Obtaining these stars allows the player to unlock more in each themed galaxy.

Mario's health consists of a power meter made of three sections, which can be restored by collecting coins. The bottomless pits featured in previous Mario games have been replaced by black holes, which are stationed beneath the surfaces of certain planets and spread throughout outside space. As always, Mario has a range of jumping abilities, such as his trademark triple jump, wall kick, ground pound, and side somersault. Some of the moves that were absent in Super Mario Sunshine have returned for this installment, such as the long jump. Mario's melee move is a spin and it allows him to attack enemies, break crystals and activate Launch Stars and Sling Stars that shoot him across the galaxy. The Wii Remote also comes into play to collect Star Bits, aim and fire them at enemies, and also to activate Pull Stars that pull Mario between planets.

#374783 12 2007-10-27T09:07:26Z tktktk
Glad to see more folks looking forward to this.

Just to illustrate how ridiculously, mind-bogglingly positive some of the impressions I've been reading are, I'm gonna post the comments I linked to, from amir0x of NeoGAF.

Now, to give some background, this isn't some googly-eyed fanboy we're talking about here. Amir0x is a mod on the GAF forums with a good reputation, he's generally critical the Wii in terms of controls and game library, and he was looking forward to Galaxy but came into it with controlled, realistic expectations.

The following is not edited, except for profanity and to emphasize certain points:

Quote: amir0x
god it's the type of game when you play, you want to wake people up just to tell them you did because it's revelatory. It's like you can FEEL the paradigm shifting under your feet when you play this, as if all Iwata's claims were proved true in an instant and the sound of a million doubters fell silent.

I am guys, you know, a HUGE Nintendo critic lately. I don't like the direction they've taken for various reasons, and I let myself be known on this issue. Everywhere. And I can say, in genuine, from the hour or so I kept coming back to the demo, that this was worth the price of Wii. I would pay $399.99 to play this.

It is almost like... jesus... it's like all those non-games were just tons and tons of crumbling rock plugging up some mighty volcano, and it all came undone with Mario Galaxy. The giant moved and swayed, melting faces in its wake. I am prone to hyperbole. I can assure you, nothing I can say will prepare.

My words may sounds hollow to some. Some more technical features: I thought wiimote would be at best a side step, as opposed to a step forward. It is comfortable, it works wonders, you do not need camera control at any moment (guys, they've designed a 3D platformer which requires NO CAMERA CONTROL EVER. Do you know what that alone indicates with the talent?). In short, it is better than traditional controls. For real. That's coming from me. Mario's momentum is just so perfectly honed that every little movement feels rewarding. You don't even have to do anything, you can just spin Mario around and around and you'll feel as giddy as a f***ing schoolchild.

This game? It LOOKS like a 360 game, save resolution. Yes, they actually did do it. Anybody tries to post LAUGHING SMILIES at this proposition, poke them in the eye with your d***. They're laughing out of fear. They've actually done it here. ANYONE on GAF that denies the visual pleasure unfolding here is a bulls*** artist and a troll. Yes, 360 can obviously do better but here is a Wii game that looks as good, and you won't even once remotely think 'oh hey if only that goomba had bump maping.'

God the design. The f***ing LEVEL design. I played much of what we've seen in early videos of this game, and even KNOWING what to expect did not truly explain what the experience is like. Here is a product that essentially s***s on all other developers from the top of some unreachable mountain top. I love Ratchet, I love Sunshine. I love platformers. So why is it that this game seems to open a door that makes me almost embarrassed to have ever lauded them? FROM AN HOUR OF PLAY.

Oh God I think I'm turning back into a Nintendo fanboy... but it's such pure joy, really encapsulate the very reason I began to play games. I feel like a new gamer.
One other thing of note; in another post he also described the game as "So good, i forgive Nintendo for not localizing Mother 3". Amir0x is so incredibly fanatical about the Mother (Earthbound) series that this might have been the most significant of all his comments.

#379054 76 2007-11-13T09:41:39Z tktktk
Quote: rocket_thumped, November 13, 2007 04:14 am
I envy you. Is it a lot like Mario64 basically?
Well, they're both 3D Mario games so there are bound to be some similarities, but it's really its own game with its own distinct gameplay mechanics. There are nods to pretty much every Mario game crammed in there, though, including Mario 64.

Quote: Ditocoaf, November 13, 2007 06:28 am
You know what depresses me? Knowing that I'll never play this game. I can't afford the time or money to get a Wii.

...come to think of it, you know what? I'm not really depressed about that. I'll live. What would depress me, is if that game was the most important thing in my life.
Hmm... are you trying to imply something?


All right, so anyway, here are the highlights of my experience so far, 20 stars in:

Visuals and music are fantastic. I don't have much to talk about as far as that goes, but yeah. Fantastic.

Camera is great. Not perfect, but great. I had no major issues and very few minor ones. Definitely a big step up from other 3D Marios, and most 3D games in general, for that matter.

The long jump and the spin move are both really useful. Long jump for crossing large gaps and traversing planets more quickly, spin move for stunning enemies and also as an extra little top-off to your jumps in case you misjudge one.

The pill-shaped planet with gravity fields in the Good Egg Galaxy had some fantastic level design. I spent a good five minutes just playing around inside it.

The first planet in the Space Junk Galaxy is really fun to jump on with the long jump. If you do it right you can go around the whole thing, and then some.

The disk-shaped planets in Battle Rock Galaxy were also fun to long jump on; I'd jump off one, swing around and end up on the opposite side of another.

Sweet Sweet Galaxy (the one with conveyor belts with shapes cut out of them) was fantastic. Just fast-paced, intense platforming. Loved it so much that when I beat it I immediately went back and played it again.

Loopdeloop Galaxy (the manta ray surfing one) was awesome. It's hard though, and I think the reason for that is because the waves are choppy and occasionally you get thrown up in the air a little bit, which at first tended to make me overcompensate on my turns. It's ridiculously fun, though, I was never genuinely frustrated.

Rolling Green Galaxy (the ball rolling one) was also awesome, and easier than the manta surfing. Some great level design here as well, with lots of different routes available for collecting stuff.

The boss battles I've played so far have for the most part been fairly easy, although still fun. The first Bowser encounter, on the other hand, was genuinely difficult.


That's it for now. As far as closing comments, I think the phrases "It's amazing" and "You should get it" sum up my feelings pretty well.

Anonymous is, put simply, a collective of internet users that plans to take down the Church of Scientology. They are not fighting against Scientology's religious doctrines, but rather the terrible crimes and immoral acts committed by the establishment of the Church itself, particularly its policy of charging hundreds of thousands of dollars for auditing courses and its "fair game" policy of destroying the lives of those it perceives to be a threat. This video is useful if you want to learn more about the crimes they have committed (just some of many). These two sites have a great deal of additional information.

By far the most ambitious phase of Project Chanology thus far is the planning of dozens of real-life protests at Scientology churches around the world at 11:00 am local time on February 10th, 2008. They've already begun as of this post, and the mainstream media has taken notice, as seen in this article regarding the protest in Sydney, Australia.

It's quite an amazing sight to behold, seeing a good portion of the internet uniting quickly and efficiently around a single cause. And the plans don't stop at February 10th; there is an elaborate long-term strategy in place, with much of the focus being placed on getting rid of Scientology's tax-exempt status, which would deal a massive blow to what is essentially a money-making scheme disguised as a religion.

If that's true, you should probably get started on taking down the Catholic Church. Same with Judaism and Buddhism. Heck, you will need to take down the leaders of Hinduism and Islam. All of these faiths have a long history including many acts of violence, oppression, murder, and sabotage. So why are you only attacking Scientology when they've hardly hurt anyone, compared to the other religions.

Furthermore, you are being hugely hypocritical with your methods. You think tyranny, threats, and blackmail will end tyranny, threats, and blackmail?
The argument of "Why take a stand against X when Y is just as bad?" is ridiculous and nonsensical. First of all, Anonymous obviously does not have the resources to protest every evil thing that goes on in the world. So it makes do with what it has.

Second, it should also be obvious that certain causes make more sense for certain groups to protest for certain reasons. In this case, Scientology makes sense for Anonymous in particular as a target because it is a fairly small organization, if still considerably threatening. The main reason there hasn't been much opposition in past years is that Scientologists will hunt down and destroy those who oppose them. But now with the internet coming into play, those protesters who were previously too afraid to speak out against the church can do so without having their identities revealed. Thus Anonymous, an internet-based group that organizes its offensive entirely online, is perfectly suited for the task.

And even if Anonymous could take down the leaders of all those religions, it really wouldn't make sense to. You seem to be ignoring the fact that for the most part none of those religions have committed any of the acts you mentioned in modern times. Honestly, why blame the current followers for the things their ancestors have done? You can point to extremist factions, but the fact is that they're just a tiny malevolent part of a benign whole.

Finally, I think it's kind of funny that you're equating all of the actions of Anonymous with me personally. I am not threatening or blackmailing anyone, thank you, and I certainly don't support those who do. What you don't seem to understand is that Anonymous is essentially a stand alone complex, probably the first one ever to emerge on the internet. In other words, rather than being a formally organized group, Anonymous is made up of individuals with individual goals and moral compasses, who happen to be working in the same general direction. One individual is not responsible for the actions of another, and frankly, couldn't do anything about them even if they wanted to. Thus, it is entirely illogical to condemn Anonymous as a whole for illegal actions performed by a handful of people.

Quote: Nemesis, February 13, 2008 06:21 pm
tktktk told me in our PM the other night that 4chan is a reasonably mature community with a substantial moral compass fighting for a noble cause. I let this go, assuming that he just didn't know what the Hell 4chan was, or is.
I just want to clear this up, for you and everyone else reading. This was not what I said you in our PM conversation. Looking back at it, the wording was slightly ambiguous, but I can assure you I'm not that naive. What I said was that Anonymous is a reasonably mature community with a substantial moral compass fighting for a noble cause. Now, I know that you still think Anonymous is essentially 4chan, but I'll get to that in a minute. First of all, I do know what 4chan is. I've read about it, I've seen it for myself on several occasions, and I know it has some absolutely horrendous stuff.

I know what it is, and I know what it can do. Which is precisely how I know that Anon isn't 4chan.

My main point is this: I have to ask you to look at the results of what has happened so far. Yes, there have been illegal activities, and that's a terrible thing. But look at what has happened since the DDoS attacks and whatever other questionable stuff has taken place. Following this video from Mark Bunker, a prominent critic of Scientology, Anonymous had a sudden change of heart. Strange that a hateful, heartless, 4chan-driven group would be so quick to change their ways, right? I have to tell you, I was personally astonished at this, and it was more or less this sudden change in tactics from Anonymous that led me to put my support behind them.

Following Mark Bunker's video, the illegal activities were promptly condemned and halted by Anonymous as a whole. There may have been a few rebels here and there, but as I've said before, aside from, say, banning them from their forums and generally shunning them from the rest of the group (which is precisely what has been done), policing them is basically impossible.

The Anonymous you described, the one made up of heartless 4channers, wouldn't have cared in the least about what Mark Bunker had to say about it, because those activities were fun for them, whether illegal or not. They would have jeered at him, cursed at him, and pretty much ripped him apart. If 4chan was really the driving force behind Anonymous at this point, as you claim, the illegal actions never would have stopped. Period.

Take Andreas Heldal-Lund, another prominent Scientology critic. I've read his website and seen videos of him conversing Scientologists, and I will say that this guy in particular is absolutely adamant about allowing free speech on both sides, Scientology as well as its critics. Initially he came out against Anonymous. Now he supports them.

Paulette Cooper, one of the first people ever to seriously criticize Scientology, recently came out in support of Anonymous as well.

So Mr. Bunker, Mr. Heldal-Lund, Ms. Cooper, and a number of other very well-respected critics now support Anon. Do you really think they would all put their reputations on the line if they didn't fully believe that Anonymous' actions were justified?

I've been reading the enturbulation.org forums, which is the essentially Anonymous' primary base of operations at this point in time. And let me tell you something. There are memes and other crap here and there, yes. But in nearly every single thread I've been in, more than anything else, the members there have been talking earnestly and passionately about helping people who are in Scientology and preventing others from experiencing the same terrible things.

I have seen countless videos and forum posts from ex-Scientologists who are incredibly grateful for what Anonymous is doing. I've even seen one or two current Scientologists, who want to get out but can't for fear of their lives, send their messages of thanks.

I've seen coverage of the protests. Estimates put the number of participants at 5,000 at the very minimum, and the true number is probably closer to 8,000 or more. Out of those thousands of people, I have heard of one incident where the police had to confront a protester. One. It was somewhere up in Canada, some idiot had brought a toy gun with him. It was promptly confiscated, and the protest went on peacefully along with the dozens of others. One guy. If Anonymous is as you say, shouldn't there have been, I don't know, mass riots?

Another thing I should mention is that I've seen that a lot of the older, "veteran" 4channers are very angry right now with how Project Chanology is being conducted. They think it's not driven by "lulz" anymore; the members of Anonymous have grown a heart and are doing this because they genuinely want to help others. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think 4channers know 4chan pretty dang well. Certainly better than you. And if they're saying that this project isn't being conducted the way 4chan is "supposed" to conduct things, I'm sort of inclined to agree with them.

You're saying that 4chan makes up the vast majority of Anonymous. But judging by the results of Project Chanology so far, which overall have been overwhelmingly positive, I have to conclude one of two things. Either 4channers have more of a heart than you seem to think, or there are more non-4channers within Anonymous than you seem to think.

Take your pick.


P.S. I may make a second post responding to the rest of yours when I have the time. In the meantime, if you choose to respond to this one, please try to keep it down to only a few miles of text this time, okay?

P.P.S. I want you to know also that I actually really appreciate your opinions on this subject and your efforts to persuade me that this cause is an unjust one, because I know that if this really was something I shouldn't be involved in, I would certainly want you to tell me. So while I disagree with you, the thought is definitely appreciated.

All right Blizz, I've read your whole megapost now. And thanks for delaying on that second post too; it took me quite some time just to get through the first one. I'm not gonna say a lot (relatively speaking), but a few things need to be addressed.

This may start to sound slightly angry at you, Blizz, but it's more that I'm confused and a little bit frustrated. Again, I appreciate you, your friendship, your concern, and everything else, but... I don't know if you're exaggerating this at all, but frankly I'm a little disturbed by your reaction to this whole debacle thus far.

First thing is, it seems like about 2% of your post was dedicated to a few passing remarks stating that 4chan is currently the driving force behind Anon. The remaining 98% was dedicated to showing us how horrible 4chan is, how their memes are somehow going to destroy these forums, how you don't want to have kids because this world is a terrible place... oh yeah, and how later on, 4chan might feel like taking down a government.

Honestly, I don't know what to say to that, except to calmly tell you that you're overreacting.

Now, I understand that 4chan in many ways really is a horrible place. I also realize 4chan is where Anon started. But as I said in my previous post, now that the rest of the internet has taken notice, non-4channers have joined in staggering numbers, and this is reflected clearly by Anon's overwhelmingly positive actions over the past two to three weeks. You can look at the brooding on the 4chan boards and hate Anonymous for it, or you can look at the actual real-life results of what Anonymous has done in these past few weeks and realize that 4chan can't be the real driving force behind Anon any longer, and that Anon is actually doing a lot of good.

One thing that I noticed you said was that Anon is growing, but it isn't being diluted; it's still just as much a monster now as it was when it was just 4chan. (This, again, despite considerable evidence to the contrary.) I have to ask, how is this even possible? Is everyone who joins a 4channer or some other sociopath? Do normal people add themselves to the ranks and immediately lose any morals they previously had? I'd like an explanation for this statement in particular, because it really does not make sense to me. Instead, what I see, what the evidence I've seen points to, is that huge numbers of ordinary internet users are joining, not to become part of some unfeeling monster, but to become part of a morally grounded cause, which did not originally exist, but, thanks to their efforts, now does. If that's not the case, kindly show me where I'm mistaken.

Now, as far as how 4chan affects these forums in particular. As I said in our PMs, I personally am perfectly alright with keeping 4chan memes banned. I really don't particularly care. And I don't think very many other people feel that strongly about it, either. You said you were allowing them, and basically I just shrugged and said, "Okay guys, you can use these now, but keep it to a reasonable level."

Instead of either accepting that, or voicing your disapproval in a way that I would normally expect you to based on these years that I've known you, you turn around and pretty much imply that the forums are about to go down in flames, "degenerate into anarchy", etc., just for want of that single rule. And you take the usernames Nemesis and Nero in some odd form of protest against... I'm not even sure what. A group that has literally no connection with these forums except through the discussion in this single thread? People being mildly disgruntled by a rule whose purpose they didn't fully understand? Your own decision to repeal that rule?

You didn't have to get rid of the 4chan rule. To be honest, you could have kept it and almost no one would really have minded. Or you could have posted explaining why you wanted the rule in place, without repealing it. That way people would have understood your reasoning, and you wouldn't have to moan about how the forums are now going to fall apart at the seams. But you didn't. Instead you spent 8 hours telling us all about how 4chan is taking over everything and now the world is going to end.

Honestly, I don't know how I'm supposed to respond to that. I really, really don't.


In any case, Blizz, I'm not going to approach this as a debate any longer, because frankly, they tend to make me feel kind of uncomfortable. If you make further mega/posts, I'll probably get around to reading them simply because I still respect your opinion on this and there's always the chance I could be wrong on one issue or another. But I probably won't give more than a few lines in response, just because these things always take me a while to write.

What I personally would suggest, Blizz, and I'm leaving this up to you:
  • Putting the 4chan rule back in place, if you care so much about it and think its absence is so dangerous, because I don't think most people mind too much. I'd rather your attitude on this not be, "No, you guys wanted it this way, so now you'll have to deal with the consequences", because as I said, I think most people either didn't feel strongly about the rule or just didn't know the reason for it.
  • Moving this thread to Serious Discussion, or splitting it between debate and more lighthearted discussion. It doesn't really feel like it belongs in just Off Topic at this point.
  • Changing your name back to Kablizzy and all that, because really, people here aren't against you the way you seem to think they are. Of course this especially is your decision, but the gloom and doom surrounding this little development in particular is really kinda depressing me.
  • Seriously, just lighten up a little, 'kay?
